description.es: Divide class into booth vendors and shoppers (will rotate) - Booth Types: * Handmade Crafts (items from CH10) * Art Gallery (items from CH11) * Paper Goods (paper treats drawn and cut from card—discuss cost of goods) * Repair Shop (Diego-style—fix broken toys or sharpen pencils for fee). Students at booths: * Arrange items * Create price tags (teacher supports: "Remember labor cost!") * Prepare for customers

description.en: Half class shops, half runs booths. Shoppers browse, decide purchases, negotiate. Vendors sell, make change, track sales. Real-time learning: "My paper cupcakes aren't selling—should I lower price?"
description.es: Half class shops, half runs booths. Shoppers browse, decide purchases, negotiate. Vendors sell, make change, track sales. Real-time learning: "My paper cupcakes aren't selling—should I lower price?"

description.en: Vendors become shoppers, shoppers become vendors. Quick inventory check: "What sold out? What didn't sell?"
description.es: Vendors become shoppers, shoppers become vendors. Quick inventory check: "What sold out? What didn't sell?"

description.en: New vendors, new shoppers. Apply learning from round 1
description.es: New vendors, new shoppers. Apply learning from round 1

description.en: Count revenue (vendors). Share purchases (shoppers). Quick discussion: "What FL concept did you use today?". Celebrate season learning!
description.es: Count revenue (vendors). Share purchases (shoppers). Quick discussion: "What FL concept did you use today?". Celebrate season learning!

discussionQuestions: My paper cupcakes aren't selling—should I lower the price?
What sold out? What didn't sell?
What FL concept did you use today?

45.label: 45 Minutes
materials: Variety of student-made items from season activities
Paper clips as coins, 50 per shopper, plus a scrap-paper budget card showing $50, collected back and reused
Price tags, receipt books, tracking sheets
Card stock and markers for paper tamales at the tamale booth (no real food)

sayThis.en: "Six booths. Crafts, art, garden, paper goods, repairs and the trading post. Vendors, set up and price everything — and every price needs a reason behind it. What it cost you to make, or what it's fairly worth in a trade. Shoppers, you'll get a turn behind a booth too."
sayThis.es: "Six booths. Crafts, art, garden, paper goods, repairs and the trading post. Vendors, set up and price everything — and every price needs a reason behind it. What it cost you to make, or what it's fairly worth in a trade. Shoppers, you'll get a turn behind a booth too."

doneWhen.en: Every booth has a sign, priced stock and a named cashier.
doneWhen.es: Every booth has a sign, priced stock and a named cashier.

watchFor.en: Prices with nothing behind them. Ask one vendor per booth to justify a price out loud before you open.
watchFor.es: Prices with nothing behind them. Ask one vendor per booth to justify a price out loud before you open.

description.en: Assign roles: * Vendors (60% of class): run booths * Shoppers (30%): browse and buy * Market Managers (10%): help resolve issues, make change, support - Booth Setup by Category: * Handmade Crafts Booth (CH10 items): beaded jewelry, ornaments, cards * Art Gallery (CH11 items): memory art (some for sale, some priceless/display only) * Garden Produce Stand: shared garden items, drawn or cut from paper. No real food. * Paper Goods Booth (cost of goods): paper treats — cookies, cupcakes and pretzels drawn and cut from card — each priced from what the card and the labor cost * Repair & Service Station (CH05): fix broken items, sharpen pencils, for fee * Trading Post (CH01): trade items without money. Vendors: * Price items (must justify: materials + labor, or fair trade value) * Arrange booth attractively * Create signs * Assign roles (cashier, sales, inventory)
description.es: Assign roles: * Vendors (60% of class): run booths * Shoppers (30%): browse and buy * Market Managers (10%): help resolve issues, make change, support - Booth Setup by Category: * Handmade Crafts Booth (CH10 items): beaded jewelry, ornaments, cards * Art Gallery (CH11 items): memory art (some for sale, some priceless/display only) * Garden Produce Stand: shared garden items, drawn or cut from paper. No real food. * Paper Goods Booth (cost of goods): paper treats — cookies, cupcakes and pretzels drawn and cut from card — each priced from what the card and the labor cost * Repair & Service Station (CH05): fix broken items, sharpen pencils, for fee * Trading Post (CH01): trade items without money. Vendors: * Price items (must justify: materials + labor, or fair trade value) * Arrange booth attractively * Create signs * Assign roles (cashier, sales, inventory)

sayThis.en: "Market's open. Shoppers — walk the whole market before you spend anything. Vendors, you can change your price whenever you like, but you'll have to say why at the close."
sayThis.es: "Market's open. Shoppers — walk the whole market before you spend anything. Vendors, you can change your price whenever you like, but you'll have to say why at the close."

doneWhen.en: Every booth has recorded at least one sale.
doneWhen.es: Every booth has recorded at least one sale.

watchFor.en: Shoppers spending everything at the first booth. Ring the bell at four minutes and move them along.
watchFor.es: Shoppers spending everything at the first booth. Ring the bell at four minutes and move them along.

description.en: Open market! Ring bell. Shoppers browse all booths. Make purchasing decisions. Vendors: * Sell items * Negotiate prices * Track inventory * Provide receipts. Market Managers circulate helping. Real market dynamics occur: * Some items sell out fast (demand!) * Perishables get discount as time passes (CH08) * Vendors adjust prices based on demand * Trades happen at Trading Post
description.es: Open market! Ring bell. Shoppers browse all booths. Make purchasing decisions. Vendors: * Sell items * Negotiate prices * Track inventory * Provide receipts. Market Managers circulate helping. Real market dynamics occur: * Some items sell out fast (demand!) * Perishables get discount as time passes (CH08) * Vendors adjust prices based on demand * Trades happen at Trading Post

sayThis.en: "Freeze. Crafts have sold out — that's demand. Garden is cutting prices, because those go off. The repair station has a queue. What does a queue tell you?"
sayThis.es: "Freeze. Crafts have sold out — that's demand. Garden is cutting prices, because those go off. The repair station has a queue. What does a queue tell you?"

doneWhen.en: Three market facts have been read out and the market is open again.
doneWhen.es: Three market facts have been read out and the market is open again.

watchFor.en: The pause turning into free time. Three announcements, then reopen.
watchFor.es: The pause turning into free time. Three announcements, then reopen.

description.en: Ring bell for brief pause. Quick announcements: * "Handmade Crafts Booth is sold out! High demand!" * "Garden Produce dropping prices—perishables!" * "Repair Station has a line—service in high demand!". Market insights create learning moments. Resume shopping
description.es: Ring bell for brief pause. Quick announcements: * "Handmade Crafts Booth is sold out! High demand!" * "Garden Produce dropping prices—perishables!" * "Repair Station has a line—service in high demand!". Market insights create learning moments. Resume shopping

sayThis.en: "Swap. Vendors are shoppers now. Before you go — one look at your stall. What sold? What didn't?"
sayThis.es: "Swap. Vendors are shoppers now. Before you go — one look at your stall. What sold? What didn't?"

doneWhen.en: Every booth has a new vendor and every former vendor is wearing a shopper badge.
doneWhen.es: Every booth has a new vendor and every former vendor is wearing a shopper badge.

watchFor.en: A slow swap eating into the second period. Count it down from ten.
watchFor.es: A slow swap eating into the second period. Count it down from ten.

description.en: Vendors and shoppers switch roles. Quick inventory: What sold? What didn't? Why?. Price adjustments for round 2
description.es: Vendors and shoppers switch roles. Quick inventory: What sold? What didn't? Why?. Price adjustments for round 2

sayThis.en: "Open. You watched the first round — use what you saw. If a price was wrong, change it."
sayThis.es: "Open. You watched the first round — use what you saw. If a price was wrong, change it."

doneWhen.en: Every booth has Period 2 sales recorded beside Period 1.
doneWhen.es: Every booth has Period 2 sales recorded beside Period 1.

watchFor.en: New vendors keeping the old prices out of politeness. Remind them the stall is theirs now.
watchFor.es: New vendors keeping the old prices out of politeness. Remind them the stall is theirs now.

description.en: Reopened market with role rotation. Apply learning from period 1. New vendors may price differently based on observations. Continued trading, buying, selling
description.es: Reopened market with role rotation. Apply learning from period 1. New vendors may price differently based on observations. Continued trading, buying, selling

sayThis.en: "Market's closed. Count your takings. Then tell me one thing you did today that you first learned in another chapter. The trading, the pricing, the repairs, the fresh-goods problem — all of it came from somewhere."
sayThis.es: "Market's closed. Count your takings. Then tell me one thing you did today that you first learned in another chapter. The trading, the pricing, the repairs, the fresh-goods problem — all of it came from somewhere."

doneWhen.en: Every booth's total is on the board and every award has been read out.
doneWhen.es: Every booth's total is on the board and every award has been read out.

watchFor.en: The answer stopping at "we sold stuff". Name one chapter yourself and let them take it from there.
watchFor.es: The answer stopping at "we sold stuff". Name one chapter yourself and let them take it from there.

description.en: Ring bell: "Market closing!". Vendors count revenue, complete tracking sheets. Shoppers review purchases - Whole-Class Discussion: * "What FL concepts did you use today?" * "What surprised you about running a market?" * "How did you decide what to buy/how to price?" * "What would you do differently next time?" - Award Ceremony (celebrating learning, not just profit): * "Best Negotiator" * "Fairest Trader" * "Most Creative Pricing" * "Kindest Vendor" * "Smartest Shopper" * Everyone gets participation certificate!
description.es: Ring bell: "Market closing!". Vendors count revenue, complete tracking sheets. Shoppers review purchases - Whole-Class Discussion: * "What FL concepts did you use today?" * "What surprised you about running a market?" * "How did you decide what to buy/how to price?" * "What would you do differently next time?" - Award Ceremony (celebrating learning, not just profit): * "Best Negotiator" * "Fairest Trader" * "Most Creative Pricing" * "Kindest Vendor" * "Smartest Shopper" * Everyone gets participation certificate!

discussionQuestions: What FL concepts did you use today?
What surprised you about running a market?
How did you decide what to buy/how to price?
What would you do differently next time?

beforeClass.en: Check each booth has stock from its own chapter: crafts from Chapter 10, art from Chapter 11, garden produce drawn on card, paper goods cut and priced. No real food at any stall. Role badges in a pile by the door.
beforeClass.es: Check each booth has stock from its own chapter: crafts from Chapter 10, art from Chapter 11, garden produce drawn on card, paper goods cut and priced. No real food at any stall. Role badges in a pile by the door.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: skip the rotation break and run one long market. Short: add a third period with one new rule — no money, trade only.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: skip the rotation break and run one long market. Short: add a third period with one new rule — no money, trade only.

standard.label: From Scratch
standard.description: Assumes the room has nothing. Season 1 kit already bought.
items: Sticky dots, 1 sheet — marking sold items
Index cards — reused from Chapter 1 for price tags and booth signs; no new purchase
Masking tape — reused from Chapter 1 for hanging the signs; no new purchase
Paper clips as coins — reused from Chapter 2; no new purchase
Inventory to sell is what students already made in Chapters 10 and 11; no purchase
Teacher backup: a box of 20 to 30 paper items kept aside from earlier chapters, for any student with nothing to sell
Student desks pushed into six booth clusters; no purchase
A bell, or any classroom object that makes a sound, to open and close the market; no purchase

lowCost.label: Basic Classroom
lowCost.description: Assumes scissors, glue, tape, pencils, paper, rulers and crayons are on hand.
items: Sticky dots, 1 sheet — marking sold items
Index cards — reused from Chapter 1; no new purchase
Paper clips as coins — reused from Chapter 2; no new purchase
Inventory to sell is what students already made in Chapters 10 and 11; no purchase
Teacher backup: a box of 20 to 30 paper items kept aside from earlier chapters

focus: *Simplifications:
Simplified market: everyone sells one item, buys one item
Round numbers only ($1, $5)
Teacher support for all transactions
Very simple tracking or none Supports:
Teacher or older buddy helps with transactions
Price tags pre-made or heavily supported
Visual cues: pictures for "buy" and "sell"
*Simplifications:
Simplified tracking sheet (just items and totals)
Pre-calculated prices available
Reduce number of booths/complexity
Pair students for support Supports:
Visual tracking sheets with pictures
Partner system: work in pairs as vendors
Step-by-step checklist for booth setup
*Simplifications:
Provide tracking sheet template
Allow calculator use
Reduce complexity: fewer booth types
Simplified award criteria Supports:
Detailed tracking worksheet with formulas
Examples of completed transactions
Small group booth teams with assigned roles
*Simplifications:
Provide formula reference cards
Reduce number of reflection questions
Allow digital tracking (spreadsheet) Supports:
Advanced tracking with built-in formulas
Access to calculators or spreadsheets
Small group vendor teams with clear leadership roles
Teacher modeling of sophisticated economic thinking

title.en: What Can YOU Make? Skills Inventory & Dream Product
title.es: What Can YOU Make? Skills Inventory & Dream Product

20.label: 20 Minutes
20.bestFor: Tight schedules, daily scheduling
20.activityName: Quick Skills Checklist & One Dream Product
materials: Simple skills checklist (pre-printed or on board)

description.en: Go through checklist together. Raise hand if you can: draw, build with blocks, cook/mix, garden, sew/craft, write stories, solve puzzles, organize things, come up with ideas, make people laugh. Students call out their top 2 skills.
description.es: Go through checklist together. Raise hand if you can: draw, build with blocks, cook/mix, garden, sew/craft, write stories, solve puzzles, organize things, come up with ideas, make people laugh. Students call out their top 2 skills.

sayThis.en: "Hands up if you can draw. Hands up if you can build with blocks. Keep going with me. Everyone can do something on this list."
sayThis.es: "Hands up if you can draw. Hands up if you can build with blocks. Keep going with me. Everyone can do something on this list."

watchFor.en: A child who never raises a hand. Name something you saw them do today — "You stacked the chairs. That's organizing."
watchFor.es: A child who never raises a hand. Name something you saw them do today — "You stacked the chairs. That's organizing."

doneWhen.en: Every child has called out or pointed to two skills.
doneWhen.es: Every child has called out or pointed to two skills.

description.en: Draw ONE product you wish you could make. Name it. Show at least one picture. Tier 1 (K-1): say the name out loud; no writing needed.
description.es: Draw ONE product you wish you could make. Name it. Show at least one picture. Tier 1 (K-1): say the name out loud; no writing needed.

sayThis.en: "Draw one thing you wish you could make. Just one. Make it big. Then tell me its name."
sayThis.es: "Draw one thing you wish you could make. Just one. Make it big. Then tell me its name."

watchFor.en: Kids drawing lots of little things. Point and ask "Which one is best?" and have them make that one big.
watchFor.es: Kids drawing lots of little things. Point and ask "Which one is best?" and have them make that one big.

doneWhen.en: Every paper has one product on it and every child can say its name.
doneWhen.es: Every paper has one product on it and every child can say its name.

description.en: Turn to partner. Show your drawing. Say: "I want to make a ___."
description.es: Turn to partner. Show your drawing. Say: "I want to make a ___."

sayThis.en: "Turn to your partner. Hold up your picture. Say: I want to make a ... Then switch."
sayThis.es: "Turn to your partner. Hold up your picture. Say: I want to make a ... Then switch."

watchFor.en: One partner talking both turns. At one minute, say "Switch."
watchFor.es: One partner talking both turns. At one minute, say "Switch."

doneWhen.en: Every child has said "I want to make a ___" to a partner.
doneWhen.es: Every child has said "I want to make a ___" to a partner.

discussionQuestions: What can you already do?
What would you like to make someday?
Who would want to buy your product?

beforeClass.en: Write the ten skills on the board so you can point at each one. Put paper, pencils and crayons on every table.
beforeClass.es: Write the ten skills on the board so you can point at each one. Put paper, pencils and crayons on every table.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: in Skills Check, skip the call-outs and go straight to Dream Product Draw. Short: in Quick Share, let two or three kids show their drawing to the whole class.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: in Skills Check, skip the call-outs and go straight to Dream Product Draw. Short: in Quick Share, let two or three kids show their drawing to the whole class.

30.label: 30 Minutes
30.bestFor: Standard class periods, weekly scheduling
30.activityName: Skills Inventory & Dream Product Design Card
materials: Skills inventory worksheet (categories: Art, Building, Writing, Numbers, Organizing, Ideas, Helping)
Examples of maker products (photos or real items)

description.en: Complete worksheet with guidance. For each category, check boxes for things you can do. Count your skills in each category. Circle your top 2 categories — these are your "maker strengths."
description.es: Complete worksheet with guidance. For each category, check boxes for things you can do. Count your skills in each category. Circle your top 2 categories — these are your "maker strengths."

sayThis.en: "Here are seven kinds of making. In each one, check every box for a thing you can do. Count your checks. Circle the two groups with the most. Those are your maker strengths."
sayThis.es: "Here are seven kinds of making. In each one, check every box for a thing you can do. Count your checks. Circle the two groups with the most. Those are your maker strengths."

watchFor.en: Kids leaving boxes blank because they think "can do" means "do really well." Say "If you've done it once, check it."
watchFor.es: Kids leaving boxes blank because they think "can do" means "do really well." Say "If you've done it once, check it."

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has checks, a count for each group and two circles.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has checks, a count for each group and two circles.

description.en: Teacher shows/discusses 5-6 maker products: painted mugs, sewn pouches, built birdhouses, decorated cookies, handmade cards, organized kits. Point out which skills each uses.
description.es: Teacher shows/discusses 5-6 maker products: painted mugs, sewn pouches, built birdhouses, decorated cookies, handmade cards, organized kits. Point out which skills each uses.

sayThis.en: "Somebody made this painted mug. What skill did they use? Art. Now this birdhouse — what skill?"
sayThis.es: "Somebody made this painted mug. What skill did they use? Art. Now this birdhouse — what skill?"

watchFor.en: Talk drifting to who has one at home. Ask "What skill made it?" and move to the next one.
watchFor.es: Talk drifting to who has one at home. Ask "What skill made it?" and move to the next one.

doneWhen.en: Five or six products are shown, each with a skill named out loud.
doneWhen.es: Five or six products are shown, each with a skill named out loud.

description.en: On design card, draw your dream product. Include: product name, what it does/who uses it, which of YOUR skills you'd use to make it, and simple price guess.
description.es: On design card, draw your dream product. Include: product name, what it does/who uses it, which of YOUR skills you'd use to make it, and simple price guess.

sayThis.en: "Draw your dream product on your card. Add four things: its name, who uses it, which of your skills you'd use, and a price guess."
sayThis.es: "Draw your dream product on your card. Add four things: its name, who uses it, which of your skills you'd use, and a price guess."

watchFor.en: Prices like a million dollars. Ask "Would a grown-up you know pay that?" and let them change it.
watchFor.es: Prices like a million dollars. Ask "Would a grown-up you know pay that?" and let them change it.

doneWhen.en: Every card has a drawing, a name, a user, a skill and a price.
doneWhen.es: Every card has a drawing, a name, a user, a skill and a price.

description.en: Post designs around room. Students walk around viewing others' ideas. Return to seats and share one product you'd want to buy from a classmate.
description.es: Post designs around room. Students walk around viewing others' ideas. Return to seats and share one product you'd want to buy from a classmate.

sayThis.en: "Tape your card up. Walk and look with your hands behind your back. Back in your seat, tell us one thing you'd buy from a friend."
sayThis.es: "Tape your card up. Walk and look with your hands behind your back. Back in your seat, tell us one thing you'd buy from a friend."

watchFor.en: A crowd at one card. Keep them moving: "Look at three, then sit."
watchFor.es: A crowd at one card. Keep them moving: "Look at three, then sit."

doneWhen.en: Every card is on the wall and a few kids have named one they'd buy.
doneWhen.es: Every card is on the wall and a few kids have named one they'd buy.

discussionQuestions: What skills are you already good at?
What skills would you like to learn this season?
How can your skills become a product?
What makes a good product idea?
Who would be your customer?
extensionIdeas: Create a class "Skills Inventory Chart" showing all students' strengths — celebrate diverse talents.

beforeClass.en: Copy the skills worksheet with seven groups — Art, Building, Writing, Numbers, Organizing, Ideas, Helping — or draw the grid on the board to copy. Set out five or six maker product photos, and tear off tape strips for the gallery walk.
beforeClass.es: Copy the skills worksheet with seven groups — Art, Building, Writing, Numbers, Organizing, Ideas, Helping — or draw the grid on the board to copy. Set out five or six maker product photos, and tear off tape strips for the gallery walk.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: in Gallery Walk & Share, skip the share back at seats and just walk. Short: in Dream Product Design, have kids add a second drawing from the side.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: in Gallery Walk & Share, skip the share back at seats and just walk. Short: in Dream Product Design, have kids add a second drawing from the side.

45.label: 45 Minutes
materials: Dream product design sheet with sketch space, specifications, target customer
Optional: sample maker products for inspiration

sayThis.en: "Ten kinds of making on the board. Score yourself one to five in every single one. One means you've never tried it. Five means people ask you to do it for them. Be honest — a low score is information, not a failure. Then circle your best three."
sayThis.es: "Ten kinds of making on the board. Score yourself one to five in every single one. One means you've never tried it. Five means people ask you to do it for them. Be honest — a low score is information, not a failure. Then circle your best three."

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has a number in all ten rows and three circled.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has a number in all ten rows and three circled.

watchFor.en: Students scoring themselves one all the way down. Ask what they did last weekend and find the skill hiding inside it.
watchFor.es: Students scoring themselves one all the way down. Ask what they did last weekend and find the skill hiding inside it.

description.en: Complete detailed inventory across categories: Visual Arts, Construction/Building, Culinary Arts, Textile/Fabric, Writing/Storytelling, Music/Performance, Organization/Planning, Problem-Solving, Technology/Digital, Nature/Gardening - Rate yourself 1-5 in each (1=beginner, 5=expert) - Calculate your top 3 skill areas - Write one sentence: "I am a maker who is good at ___, ___, and ___." Tier 1 (K-1): raise a hand for each skill you have, then say your best one to a partner.
description.es: Complete detailed inventory across categories: Visual Arts, Construction/Building, Culinary Arts, Textile/Fabric, Writing/Storytelling, Music/Performance, Organization/Planning, Problem-Solving, Technology/Digital, Nature/Gardening - Rate yourself 1-5 in each (1=beginner, 5=expert) - Calculate your top 3 skill areas - Write one sentence: "I am a maker who is good at ___, ___, and ___." Tier 1 (K-1): raise a hand for each skill you have, then say your best one to a partner.

sayThis.en: "Five ideas. Not five good ones — five. Bad ideas are how you get to the good one. Then cross out four."
sayThis.es: "Five ideas. Not five good ones — five. Bad ideas are how you get to the good one. Then cross out four."

doneWhen.en: Every sheet shows five ideas with four crossed out.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet shows five ideas with four crossed out.

watchFor.en: Students stopping at one idea and defending it. Hold the line at five before anybody chooses.
watchFor.es: Students stopping at one idea and defending it. Hold the line at five before anybody chooses.

description.en: Review example products that use skills similar to yours - Brainstorm 5 possible products you could make using your skills - Choose the ONE you're most excited about
description.es: Review example products that use skills similar to yours - Brainstorm 5 possible products you could make using your skills - Choose the ONE you're most excited about

sayThis.en: "Draw it from two sides, not one. Give it a name. Then three answers: what it does, who needs it, what you'd charge. Last line — what would you have to learn to actually make this?"
sayThis.es: "Draw it from two sides, not one. Give it a name. Then three answers: what it does, who needs it, what you'd charge. Last line — what would you have to learn to actually make this?"

doneWhen.en: Every design has a name, two drawings, a named customer and a price.
doneWhen.es: Every design has a name, two drawings, a named customer and a price.

watchFor.en: Drawings with no materials named. Ask what it's made of and where that comes from.
watchFor.es: Drawings with no materials named. Ask what it's made of and where that comes from.

description.en: Sketch your product from multiple angles - Name it (be creative!) - Write description: What is it? What does it do? Who needs it? - Identify target customer (age, interests, why they'd buy it) - Estimate: Materials needed, time to make one, price you'd charge - Note: What skills do you already have? What would you need to learn? Tier 1 (K-1): draw the product and tell a partner its name and who it is for.
description.es: Sketch your product from multiple angles - Name it (be creative!) - Write description: What is it? What does it do? Who needs it? - Identify target customer (age, interests, why they'd buy it) - Estimate: Materials needed, time to make one, price you'd charge - Note: What skills do you already have? What would you need to learn? Tier 1 (K-1): draw the product and tell a partner its name and who it is for.

sayThis.en: "Thirty seconds. Who you are, what you're good at, what you made, who it's for. Then stop. Thirty seconds is shorter than you think, and I'm timing it."
sayThis.es: "Thirty seconds. Who you are, what you're good at, what you made, who it's for. Then stop. Thirty seconds is shorter than you think, and I'm timing it."

doneWhen.en: Every student has pitched to a partner and at least six have pitched to the room.
doneWhen.es: Every student has pitched to a partner and at least six have pitched to the room.

watchFor.en: Pitches that describe the drawing instead of the customer. Ask "who buys it?" once, mid-pitch.
watchFor.es: Pitches that describe the drawing instead of the customer. Ask "who buys it?" once, mid-pitch.

description.en: Using template, write 30-second pitch: "Hi, I'm [name]. I'm a maker who can [skills]. I designed [product] for people who [need]. I'm excited to make this because [reason]." - Practice with partner - 6-8 volunteers present to class. Tier 1 (K-1): say the pitch out loud with the frame; no writing.
description.es: Using template, write 30-second pitch: "Hi, I'm [name]. I'm a maker who can [skills]. I designed [product] for people who [need]. I'm excited to make this because [reason]." - Practice with partner - 6-8 volunteers present to class. Tier 1 (K-1): say the pitch out loud with the frame; no writing.

sayThis.en: "One compliment each, and it has to be about the product, not the person. Then finish the line on your sheet: after today, I'm excited to make blank."
sayThis.es: "One compliment each, and it has to be about the product, not the person. Then finish the line on your sheet: after today, I'm excited to make blank."

doneWhen.en: Every presenter has had one compliment and every sheet's last line is filled.
doneWhen.es: Every presenter has had one compliment and every sheet's last line is filled.

watchFor.en: "It was good" as the compliment. Ask what was good about it.
watchFor.es: "It was good" as the compliment. Ask what was good about it.

description.en: Classmates give one compliment per pitch - Self-reflection: "After today, I'm excited to make ___."
description.es: Classmates give one compliment per pitch - Self-reflection: "After today, I'm excited to make ___."

discussionQuestions: How did identifying your skills help you think of product ideas?
What's the difference between a skill and a product?
Why do different people have different maker skills?
If you don't have all the skills yet, can you still be a maker? (YES!)
How do you turn an idea into something you can actually make?
What makes a product worth buying?
extensionIdeas: Create digital "Maker Profile" posters to display
Research real makers in your community and their skills
Start a "Skill Swap" where students teach each other (art kid teaches drawing, building kid teaches construction)

20.label: 20 Minutes
20.bestFor: Tight schedules, daily scheduling

description.en: Teacher shows careful folding technique. Emphasize: "Watch closely. Precision matters."
description.es: Teacher shows careful folding technique. Emphasize: "Watch closely. Precision matters."

sayThis.en: "Watch my hands. I line up the corners. I press the fold flat. I go slow. Careful folds come out right."
sayThis.es: "Watch my hands. I line up the corners. I press the fold flat. I go slow. Careful folds come out right."

watchFor.en: Kids folding along before you finish. Papers stay flat on the desk until you say go.
watchFor.es: Kids folding along before you finish. Papers stay flat on the desk until you say go.

doneWhen.en: You have shown every fold once.
doneWhen.es: You have shown every fold once.

description.en: Students follow instructions to fold paper into specific shape (paper airplane, origami cup, or simple box). Teacher circulates, doesn't intervene.
description.es: Students follow instructions to fold paper into specific shape (paper airplane, origami cup, or simple box). Teacher circulates, doesn't intervene.

sayThis.en: "Now you fold. Corners together, press flat, one step at a time. I'm watching, but I won't help."
sayThis.es: "Now you fold. Corners together, press flat, one step at a time. I'm watching, but I won't help."

watchFor.en: Kids asking you to fix theirs. Say "Do your best. We'll look at them together."
watchFor.es: Kids asking you to fix theirs. Say "Do your best. We'll look at them together."

doneWhen.en: Every child has a finished fold, right or wrong.
doneWhen.es: Every child has a finished fold, right or wrong.

description.en: Hold up results. Compare to teacher's model. How many match exactly? Discuss what happened when steps were rushed or measurements were off.
description.es: Hold up results. Compare to teacher's model. How many match exactly? Discuss what happened when steps were rushed or measurements were off.

sayThis.en: "Hold yours up next to mine. Does it match? Where is it different?"
sayThis.es: "Hold yours up next to mine. Does it match? Where is it different?"

watchFor.en: Kids laughing at crooked ones. Say "Crooked shows us where the fold went wrong. That helps."
watchFor.es: Kids laughing at crooked ones. Say "Crooked shows us where the fold went wrong. That helps."

doneWhen.en: Every fold is held up and a few kids have said where theirs went off.
doneWhen.es: Every fold is held up and a few kids have said where theirs went off.

description.en: "What happens if you don't measure/fold carefully?" Connect to: carpenters can't unfold wood once it's cut.
description.es: "What happens if you don't measure/fold carefully?" Connect to: carpenters can't unfold wood once it's cut.

sayThis.en: "You can open paper and fold it again. If a carpenter cuts wood wrong, can they fix it? No. So what should they do first?"
sayThis.es: "You can open paper and fold it again. If a carpenter cuts wood wrong, can they fix it? No. So what should they do first?"

watchFor.en: Kids saying "just glue it." Say "Glue shows. The buyer can see it."
watchFor.es: Kids saying "just glue it." Say "Glue shows. The buyer can see it."

doneWhen.en: Kids can say "go slow" or "check first."
doneWhen.es: Kids can say "go slow" or "check first."

discussionQuestions: Did your paper look like the example?
What happened if you folded in the wrong place?
Can you unfold and start over with paper? Can you with wood?

beforeClass.en: Fold one model ahead of time — a paper cup is the quickest — and keep it to hold up. Put one sheet of paper on every desk.
beforeClass.es: Fold one model ahead of time — a paper cup is the quickest — and keep it to hold up. Put one sheet of paper on every desk.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: in Comparison, hold up five papers instead of everyone's. Short: in Reflection, also ask what each child would do differently on a second try.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: in Comparison, hold up five papers instead of everyone's. Short: in Reflection, also ask what each child would do differently on a second try.

30.label: 30 Minutes
30.bestFor: Standard class periods, weekly scheduling
materials: Cardboard sheets (one per student or pair)
Template with exact dimensions (e.g., "Cut rectangle: 4 inches x 6 inches")

description.en: Show template with measurements. Students must create exact rectangle by measuring and cutting. Review ruler use. Emphasize: "Measure twice, cut once."
description.es: Show template with measurements. Students must create exact rectangle by measuring and cutting. Review ruler use. Emphasize: "Measure twice, cut once."

sayThis.en: "Your rectangle is 4 inches by 6 inches. Put the zero on your ruler at the edge. Measure twice, cut once. Nobody cuts until I check."
sayThis.es: "Your rectangle is 4 inches by 6 inches. Put the zero on your ruler at the edge. Measure twice, cut once. Nobody cuts until I check."

watchFor.en: Kids starting at the 1 instead of the 0. Hold up your ruler and point to the zero.
watchFor.es: Kids starting at the 1 instead of the 0. Hold up your ruler and point to the zero.

doneWhen.en: Every student can point to the zero on their ruler.
doneWhen.es: Every student can point to the zero on their ruler.

description.en: Students measure carefully and mark cutting lines on cardboard. Teacher checks measurements before anyone cuts. Tier 1 (K-1): trace a ready-made template instead of measuring.
description.es: Students measure carefully and mark cutting lines on cardboard. Teacher checks measurements before anyone cuts. Tier 1 (K-1): trace a ready-made template instead of measuring.

sayThis.en: "Measure 4 inches. Make a dot. Measure again. Now 6 inches. Join the dots with the ruler. Hands up when you're ready for me to check."
sayThis.es: "Measure 4 inches. Make a dot. Measure again. Now 6 inches. Join the dots with the ruler. Hands up when you're ready for me to check."

watchFor.en: Lines drawn without the ruler. Have them lay the ruler down and draw along it.
watchFor.es: Lines drawn without the ruler. Have them lay the ruler down and draw along it.

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has four lines you have checked.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has four lines you have checked.

description.en: Students cut along marked lines.
description.es: Students cut along marked lines.

sayThis.en: "Cut right on the line, slowly. Turn the cardboard, not the scissors. Scraps go in the box."
sayThis.es: "Cut right on the line, slowly. Turn the cardboard, not the scissors. Scraps go in the box."

watchFor.en: Scissors drifting off the line at corners. Stop, turn the cardboard, start again on the line.
watchFor.es: Scissors drifting off the line at corners. Stop, turn the cardboard, start again on the line.

doneWhen.en: Every student has a cut rectangle and their scraps are in the box.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a cut rectangle and their scraps are in the box.

description.en: Measure finished rectangles. Award "Precision Points" for pieces within 1/4 inch of target. Display results: how many were accurate? Tier 1 (K-1): lay the template on top and check if the edges match.
description.es: Measure finished rectangles. Award "Precision Points" for pieces within 1/4 inch of target. Display results: how many were accurate? Tier 1 (K-1): lay the template on top and check if the edges match.

sayThis.en: "Swap with a partner. Measure their rectangle. Within a quarter inch of 4 by 6 gets a Precision Point."
sayThis.es: "Swap with a partner. Measure their rectangle. Within a quarter inch of 4 by 6 gets a Precision Point."

watchFor.en: Partners arguing over a tiny gap. You make the call and move on.
watchFor.es: Partners arguing over a tiny gap. You make the call and move on.

doneWhen.en: Every rectangle is measured and the count of accurate ones is on the board.
doneWhen.es: Every rectangle is measured and the count of accurate ones is on the board.

description.en: Show pile of scrap cardboard. "This is waste. If cardboard costs $1 per sheet and we wasted 30% making mistakes, we spent $0.30 extra. In a business, that adds up." Calculate class waste. Tier 1 (K-1): count the scrap pieces together; skip the percent.
description.es: Show pile of scrap cardboard. "This is waste. If cardboard costs $1 per sheet and we wasted 30% making mistakes, we spent $0.30 extra. In a business, that adds up." Calculate class waste. Tier 1 (K-1): count the scrap pieces together; skip the percent.

sayThis.en: "Look at the scrap box. We paid for every piece in it. If one sheet costs one dollar, how much did we throw away?"
sayThis.es: "Look at the scrap box. We paid for every piece in it. If one sheet costs one dollar, how much did we throw away?"

watchFor.en: Kids thinking scrap is free. Hold up a scrap and ask what the whole sheet cost.
watchFor.es: Kids thinking scrap is free. Hold up a scrap and ask what the whole sheet cost.

doneWhen.en: The class has counted the waste and said out loud what it cost.
doneWhen.es: The class has counted the waste and said out loud what it cost.

discussionQuestions: How many got the exact measurements?
What mistakes did you make?
How much cardboard did we waste?
If you were selling these, would mistakes cost you money?
extensionIdeas: Build simple box from measured cardboard pieces—precision matters for fit.

beforeClass.en: Write the target size on the board — for example, 4 inches by 6 inches — and draw the rectangle. Put a ruler, pencil, safety scissors and one cardboard sheet at each seat, with a scrap box at the front.
beforeClass.es: Write the target size on the board — for example, 4 inches by 6 inches — and draw the rectangle. Put a ruler, pencil, safety scissors and one cardboard sheet at each seat, with a scrap box at the front.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: in Quality Check, measure five pieces as a class instead of every piece. Short: in Waste Discussion, have kids measure and cut a second rectangle from their scrap.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: in Quality Check, measure five pieces as a class instead of every piece. Short: in Waste Discussion, have kids measure and cut a second rectangle from their scrap.

45.label: 45 Minutes
materials: Rulers, pencils, scissors (or safe cutting tools)
"Materials budget" written on a scrap-paper card, crossed out and rewritten as it is spent
Waste tracking and cost calculation worksheets

sayThis.en: "Ten dollars on your card. Cardboard is two dollars a sheet. Here's exactly the size you're building. Every mistake costs another sheet, and another two dollars. Measure twice, cut once. Today that isn't a saying, it's the rules."
sayThis.es: "Ten dollars on your card. Cardboard is two dollars a sheet. Here's exactly the size you're building. Every mistake costs another sheet, and another two dollars. Measure twice, cut once. Today that isn't a saying, it's the rules."

doneWhen.en: Every team has $10 written on its card and the spec copied down.
doneWhen.es: Every team has $10 written on its card and the spec copied down.

watchFor.en: Teams treating the money as pretend. Say plainly what happens at zero: you stop building.
watchFor.es: Teams treating the money as pretend. Say plainly what happens at zero: you stop building.

description.en: Each team writes $10 at the top of a scrap-paper budget card; Cardboard costs $2 per sheet, crossed off the card at purchase; Challenge: Build structure to exact specifications (e.g., box that's 5"x5"x3"); Every mistake = buy new materials = less left on the card; Goal: Build to spec with minimal waste
description.es: Each team writes $10 at the top of a scrap-paper budget card; Cardboard costs $2 per sheet, crossed off the card at purchase; Challenge: Build structure to exact specifications (e.g., box that's 5"x5"x3"); Every mistake = buy new materials = less left on the card; Goal: Build to spec with minimal waste

sayThis.en: "Nothing gets cut until I've seen the plan. Draw the sheet, draw your cuts on it, count your pieces. Fit them so the scraps come out small."
sayThis.es: "Nothing gets cut until I've seen the plan. Draw the sheet, draw your cuts on it, count your pieces. Fit them so the scraps come out small."

doneWhen.en: Every team's cutting diagram has your approval before materials are handed out.
doneWhen.es: Every team's cutting diagram has your approval before materials are handed out.

watchFor.en: Plans with no measurements on them. Send it back once. That's cheaper than a wasted sheet.
watchFor.es: Plans with no measurements on them. Send it back once. That's cheaper than a wasted sheet.

description.en: Teams plan their cuts on paper first; Calculate how many pieces needed and measurements; Draw cutting diagram to minimize waste; Teacher approves plan before materials are distributed
description.es: Teams plan their cuts on paper first; Calculate how many pieces needed and measurements; Draw cutting diagram to minimize waste; Teacher approves plan before materials are distributed

sayThis.en: "Measure, mark, then cut. Every scrap goes in your own pile, not the bin — we're measuring and counting the waste at the end. I'm not going to help. That's on purpose."
sayThis.es: "Measure, mark, then cut. Every scrap goes in your own pile, not the bin — we're measuring and counting the waste at the end. I'm not going to help. That's on purpose."

doneWhen.en: Every team has a built structure and its own pile of scrap on the desk.
doneWhen.es: Every team has a built structure and its own pile of scrap on the desk.

watchFor.en: Your own urge to step in when a team cuts wrong. Don't. Note it and let them buy another sheet.
watchFor.es: Your own urge to step in when a team cuts wrong. Don't. Note it and let them buy another sheet.

description.en: Teams measure carefully, mark, and cut; Track every piece of waste on worksheet; Build structure according to specs; Teacher circulates, doesn't help—mistakes are learning. Tier 1 (K-1): trace a ready-made template and cut on the lines.
description.es: Teams measure carefully, mark, and cut; Track every piece of waste on worksheet; Build structure according to specs; Teacher circulates, doesn't help—mistakes are learning. Tier 1 (K-1): trace a ready-made template and cut on the lines.

sayThis.en: "Ruler on it. Within a quarter inch is full points. Everything gets measured, including the one I made."
sayThis.es: "Ruler on it. Within a quarter inch is full points. Everything gets measured, including the one I made."

doneWhen.en: Every structure has a measured score written on it and its scrap tallied.
doneWhen.es: Every structure has a measured score written on it and its scrap tallied.

watchFor.en: Teams measuring their own work and rounding kindly. Swap the builds so nobody inspects their own.
watchFor.es: Teams measuring their own work and rounding kindly. Swap the builds so nobody inspects their own.

description.en: Measure finished structures against specs; Award "precision points" for accuracy (within 1/4 inch = full points); Calculate waste: measure scrap pieces, tally total. Tier 1 (K-1): lay the template on top and check if the edges match.
description.es: Measure finished structures against specs; Award "precision points" for accuracy (within 1/4 inch = full points); Calculate waste: measure scrap pieces, tally total. Tier 1 (K-1): lay the template on top and check if the edges match.

sayThis.en: "How much did you spend? How much scrap have you got? Both numbers go on the board. The team that hit the spec and spent least is the team that made money."
sayThis.es: "How much did you spend? How much scrap have you got? Both numbers go on the board. The team that hit the spec and spent least is the team that made money."

doneWhen.en: Every team's spend and waste percentage is on the class graph.
doneWhen.es: Every team's spend and waste percentage is on the class graph.

watchFor.en: Waste being treated as a joke. Point at the money: every one of those scraps was part of a two-dollar sheet.
watchFor.es: Waste being treated as a joke. Point at the money: every one of those scraps was part of a two-dollar sheet.

description.en: Calculate cost: materials purchased, waste generated; If structure meets specs with minimal waste = "profit"; If excessive waste or structure doesn't meet specs = "loss"; Graph class results: waste % vs. success rate. Tier 1 (K-1): count the sheets bought and the scrap pieces; no percents.
description.es: Calculate cost: materials purchased, waste generated; If structure meets specs with minimal waste = "profit"; If excessive waste or structure doesn't meet specs = "loss"; Graph class results: waste % vs. success rate. Tier 1 (K-1): count the sheets bought and the scrap pieces; no percents.

discussionQuestions: "What was your biggest challenge in measuring precisely?"
"How much material did you waste? What did that cost?"
"If you could do it again, what would you change?"
"How does precision affect profit in real businesses?"
"Why do builders and carpenters measure so carefully?"
"What's the difference between 'good enough' and 'exact'?"
extensionIdeas: Second round with same challenge—track improvement
Design your own structure and create specs for others to build
Calculate % waste across class—what's acceptable? What's too much?
Research: how do real factories minimize waste?
Visit hardware store to price materials and understand real costs

beforeClass.en: Cut the cardboard into same-size sheets and count them. Write the exact build spec on the board so nobody works from memory. Decide now that you will not help during the build; the mistakes are the lesson.
beforeClass.es: Cut the cardboard into same-size sheets and count them. Write the exact build spec on the board so nobody works from memory. Decide now that you will not help during the build; the mistakes are the lesson.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: spot-check the inspection yourself instead of measuring every build. Short: add a second build to spec using whatever money each team has left.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: spot-check the inspection yourself instead of measuring every build. Short: add a second build to spec using whatever money each team has left.

standard.label: From Scratch
standard.description: Clean card stock, tape and budget cards. The practice cardboard is free
items: Chipboard or cereal-box card, 1 pack of 25 sheets — $4.00. Cuts cleaner and straighter than shipping cardboard, which matters when the lesson is precision
Masking tape, 2 rolls, covers this chapter and Chapter 8 — $3.00
Index cards, 1 pack of 100, for the $10 budget cards — $2.00
Shipping boxes, flattened, about 12 sheets roughly 12 inches square — free. The school office and the cafeteria both throw boxes away weekly. Ask once and keep a standing stack
Cutting diagram drawn on scrap paper before any cutting
Waste tally sheet drawn on the board and copied
A box to collect scrap for counting at the end — free, use a delivery box
Rulers, scissors and pencils from the Season 1 kit
Copy paper — 1 sheet per student for the folding challenge, from the Chapter 1 ream

lowCost.label: Basic Classroom
lowCost.description: Card stock and budget cards. The room supplies the tools and the tape
items: Chipboard or cereal-box card, 1 pack of 25 sheets — $4.00
Index cards, 1 pack of 100, for the $10 budget cards — $2.00
Shipping boxes, flattened, about 12 sheets — free from the office and the cafeteria
A box to collect scrap for counting at the end — free
Rulers, scissors, pencils and tape from the classroom supply
Copy paper from the classroom supply — 1 sheet per student for the folding challenge
Scrap paper for the cutting diagram and the waste tally — free, from the recycling bin

focus: Simple folding or single-cut challenges
Visual templates with clear pictures
Focus on "careful work" concept, less on exact measurements
Teacher helps with ruler reading
Basic vocabulary: measure, cut, careful, match
Measure to nearest inch or half-inch
Simple shapes with 2-3 measurements
Can identify and explain one mistake
Use sentence frames: "I measured ___ inches. I need to cut ___."
Vocabulary: ruler, inch, precise, waste, specification
Measure to quarter-inch
Multi-step construction with several measurements
Track waste and understand its cost impact
Can explain precision-profit connection
Vocabulary: accuracy, tolerance, quality control, defect
Measure to eighth-inch or use metric
Complex builds requiring planning and multiple precise cuts
Calculate waste percentage and cost
Understand quality standards and specifications
Advanced vocabulary: tolerance, specification, calibration, efficiency, profit margin

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Show each move — ruler at zero, dot, line, cut — with your hands before you say it.
Draw the target shape on the board with the numbers on its sides.
Give the frame "I measured ___ inches. I need to cut ___."

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Give a pre-marked line or a template to trace, so the student practices cutting, not measuring.
Put a sticker on the ruler's zero and on the target inch mark.
Pair the student with a partner who holds the ruler still while they mark.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Write your own build spec and trade it with another team to build.
Work out what the waste would cost if every sheet cost twice as much.
Find a cutting plan that gets the most pieces from one sheet, and prove it with a drawing.

20.label: 20 Minutes
20.bestFor: Tight schedules, daily scheduling
materials: Brown paper bags (2 per demo, or 2 per student)
Small item to "package" (a toy, a pencil, an eraser — anything the room already has)

description.en: Discuss packaging: protects product, makes it attractive, tells information. Show examples of good packaging. Explain design challenge: create package for a simple product.
description.es: Discuss packaging: protects product, makes it attractive, tells information. Show examples of good packaging. Explain design challenge: create package for a simple product.

sayThis.en: "A package does three jobs. It keeps the thing safe. It makes it look nice. It tells you what's inside. Look at this box — what does it tell you?"
sayThis.es: "A package does three jobs. It keeps the thing safe. It makes it look nice. It tells you what's inside. Look at this box — what does it tell you?"

watchFor.en: Kids reading every word on the box. Pick one thing it tells you and move on.
watchFor.es: Kids reading every word on the box. Pick one thing it tells you and move on.

doneWhen.en: The class has named the three jobs.
doneWhen.es: The class has named the three jobs.

description.en: Students choose a simple product to package (real or pretend): toy, craft, food item. Sketch package ideas. Plan: What shape? What information? What colors? How to make it attractive? Tier 1 (K-1): pick a product, draw it, and say one color you will use.
description.es: Students choose a simple product to package (real or pretend): toy, craft, food item. Sketch package ideas. Plan: What shape? What information? What colors? How to make it attractive? Tier 1 (K-1): pick a product, draw it, and say one color you will use.

sayThis.en: "Pick one thing to put in a package. It can be real or pretend. Draw some ideas. What shape? What colors? What words go on it?"
sayThis.es: "Pick one thing to put in a package. It can be real or pretend. Draw some ideas. What shape? What colors? What words go on it?"

watchFor.en: Kids who can't pick a product. Offer three: a toy, a cookie, a pencil.
watchFor.es: Kids who can't pick a product. Offer three: a toy, a cookie, a pencil.

doneWhen.en: Every child has picked a product and drawn at least one package idea.
doneWhen.es: Every child has picked a product and drawn at least one package idea.

description.en: Students draw detailed package design on paper: all sides, labels, how it opens. Include product name and key information. Tier 1 (K-1): draw the front of the package; the teacher writes the name.
description.es: Students draw detailed package design on paper: all sides, labels, how it opens. Include product name and key information. Tier 1 (K-1): draw the front of the package; the teacher writes the name.

sayThis.en: "Pick your best idea. Draw it again, bigger. Put the name on it. Show how it opens."
sayThis.es: "Pick your best idea. Draw it again, bigger. Put the name on it. Show how it opens."

watchFor.en: Kids starting a brand-new idea. Point back to their best one.
watchFor.es: Kids starting a brand-new idea. Point back to their best one.

doneWhen.en: Every paper has one package drawing with a name on it.
doneWhen.es: Every paper has one package drawing with a name on it.

description.en: Students build simple package prototype from cardboard, paper, or recycled materials. Focus on basic structure and functionality. Tier 1 (K-1): decorate a box that is already made instead of building one.
description.es: Students build simple package prototype from cardboard, paper, or recycled materials. Focus on basic structure and functionality. Tier 1 (K-1): decorate a box that is already made instead of building one.

sayThis.en: "Now build it from your box or paper. It just has to hold your thing and close."
sayThis.es: "Now build it from your box or paper. It just has to hold your thing and close."

watchFor.en: Kids decorating before it holds together. Ask "Does it close?" first.
watchFor.es: Kids decorating before it holds together. Ask "Does it close?" first.

doneWhen.en: Every child has a package that holds together.
doneWhen.es: Every child has a package that holds together.

description.en: Students present packages in small groups. Explain design choices: Why this shape? What makes it attractive? What information is important? Get peer feedback on design. Tier 1 (K-1): show your package and say one thing you like about it.
description.es: Students present packages in small groups. Explain design choices: Why this shape? What makes it attractive? What information is important? Get peer feedback on design. Tier 1 (K-1): show your package and say one thing you like about it.

sayThis.en: "In your group, show your package. Say why you picked the shape and colors. Friends, say one thing you like and one thing to try."
sayThis.es: "In your group, show your package. Say why you picked the shape and colors. Friends, say one thing you like and one thing to try."

watchFor.en: Feedback like "it's bad." Give the frame "I like ___. You could try ___."
watchFor.es: Feedback like "it's bad." Give the frame "I like ___. You could try ___."

doneWhen.en: Every child has shown a package and heard one like and one idea.
doneWhen.es: Every child has shown a package and heard one like and one idea.

discussionQuestions: Which package in your group looked most special?
Would you pay more for something in a nice package?
Why does packaging matter?

beforeClass.en: Pull two or three real packages from the recycling bin, like a cereal box and a gift bag. Put scrap paper, crayons, glue and a box or scrap card at each table.
beforeClass.es: Pull two or three real packages from the recycling bin, like a cereal box and a gift bag. Put scrap paper, crayons, glue and a box or scrap card at each table.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: in Package Presentation, have each child give one reason instead of answering every question. Short: in Packaging Prototype Sketch, have kids draw the back of the package too.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: in Package Presentation, have each child give one reason instead of answering every question. Short: in Packaging Prototype Sketch, have kids draw the back of the package too.

30.label: 30 Minutes
30.bestFor: Standard class periods, weekly scheduling
materials: Simple box templates (pre-scored or flat boxes to assemble)
Small item for each student to package
"Brand Planning" worksheet (name, logo sketch, color choice)

description.en: Students complete worksheet: What's your brand name? (can be your own name + "Creations"). Sketch simple logo. Choose 2-3 brand colors. Tier 1 (K-1): draw a logo and pick colors; the teacher writes the name.
description.es: Students complete worksheet: What's your brand name? (can be your own name + "Creations"). Sketch simple logo. Choose 2-3 brand colors. Tier 1 (K-1): draw a logo and pick colors; the teacher writes the name.

sayThis.en: "Every brand needs a name. You can use your own name plus Creations. Draw a logo you can draw fast. Pick two or three colors."
sayThis.es: "Every brand needs a name. You can use your own name plus Creations. Draw a logo you can draw fast. Pick two or three colors."

watchFor.en: Kids stuck on a name. Give the frame: your name plus Creations.
watchFor.es: Kids stuck on a name. Give the frame: your name plus Creations.

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has a name, a logo and colors picked.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has a name, a logo and colors picked.

description.en: Fold pre-scored boxes or assemble simple boxes from template. Tier 1 (K-1): use a box that is already folded.
description.es: Fold pre-scored boxes or assemble simple boxes from template. Tier 1 (K-1): use a box that is already folded.

sayThis.en: "Fold on the lines. Tuck the flaps in. Glue only if it won't stay shut."
sayThis.es: "Fold on the lines. Tuck the flaps in. Glue only if it won't stay shut."

watchFor.en: Boxes folded inside out. Check one fold before they do the rest.
watchFor.es: Boxes folded inside out. Check one fold before they do the rest.

doneWhen.en: Every student has a box that stands up and closes.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a box that stands up and closes.

description.en: Transfer brand name and logo to box. Use brand colors. Add decorative elements. Make it look "store quality."
description.es: Transfer brand name and logo to box. Use brand colors. Add decorative elements. Make it look "store quality."

sayThis.en: "Put your name and logo on the box. Use only your brand colors. Make it look like it came from a store."
sayThis.es: "Put your name and logo on the box. Use only your brand colors. Make it look like it came from a store."

watchFor.en: Kids using every color in the set. Point to the colors on their worksheet.
watchFor.es: Kids using every color in the set. Point to the colors on their worksheet.

doneWhen.en: Every box shows the brand name, the logo and the brand colors.
doneWhen.es: Every box shows the brand name, the logo and the brand colors.

description.en: Teacher shows same item in plain box vs decorated box. Class votes which they'd buy. Discuss why packaging matters.
description.es: Teacher shows same item in plain box vs decorated box. Class votes which they'd buy. Discuss why packaging matters.

sayThis.en: "Same thing in both boxes. Which one would you buy? Hands up. Why does the box change your mind?"
sayThis.es: "Same thing in both boxes. Which one would you buy? Hands up. Why does the box change your mind?"

watchFor.en: Kids voting for both. Make them pick one.
watchFor.es: Kids voting for both. Make them pick one.

doneWhen.en: The vote is counted and someone has said why the box matters.
doneWhen.es: The vote is counted and someone has said why the box matters.

discussionQuestions: What makes packaging look professional?
If two products are the same but one has better packaging, which costs more?
How much would you pay for your product in plain packaging? In your branded packaging?
What does your packaging say about your product?
extensionIdeas: "Shopping" activity where students browse each other's packaged products and note which ones attract them most.

beforeClass.en: Put the same small item in a plain box and in a decorated box for the Comparison Test. Put a flat box, markers and a brand worksheet or scrap paper at each seat.
beforeClass.es: Put the same small item in a plain box and in a decorated box for the Comparison Test. Put a flat box, markers and a brand worksheet or scrap paper at each seat.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: in Design & Decorate, have kids finish the front and one side only. Short: in Comparison Test, let the class vote on a few student boxes too.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: in Design & Decorate, have kids finish the front and one side only. Short: in Comparison Test, let the class vote on a few student boxes too.

45.label: 45 Minutes
45.activityName: Complete Packaging Design Challenge with Cost Analysis
materials: Box-building materials (cardboard, templates, or flat boxes)
Full art supply set (markers, colored pencils, stickers, ribbons, stamps)
Product for packaging (can be something students made earlier, or provided item)

sayThis.en: "A brand is four things. A name. A line that says what you're about. A mark you can draw in two seconds. And two colors. Pick your customer first — a box for a six-year-old looks nothing like a box for a grandad."
sayThis.es: "A brand is four things. A name. A line that says what you're about. A mark you can draw in two seconds. And two colors. Pick your customer first — a box for a six-year-old looks nothing like a box for a grandad."

doneWhen.en: Every student has a name, a tagline, a logo and two named colors on the page.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a name, a tagline, a logo and two named colors on the page.

watchFor.en: Logos that take five minutes to draw. Make them draw it three times in a row; it gets simpler every time.
watchFor.es: Logos that take five minutes to draw. Make them draw it three times in a row; it gets simpler every time.

description.en: Create complete brand identity: business name, tagline, logo, color palette; Design packaging that reflects brand; Consider target customer: "Who will buy this? What do they like?" Tier 1 (K-1): pick a name and two colors and draw a picture logo; the teacher writes the name.
description.es: Create complete brand identity: business name, tagline, logo, color palette; Design packaging that reflects brand; Consider target customer: "Who will buy this? What do they like?" Tier 1 (K-1): pick a name and two colors and draw a picture logo; the teacher writes the name.

sayThis.en: "Every side of the box gets something. Nobody only ever sees the front. Then one finishing touch inside — a note, a ribbon, a thank you. That's the bit people remember."
sayThis.es: "Every side of the box gets something. Nobody only ever sees the front. Then one finishing touch inside — a note, a ribbon, a thank you. That's the bit people remember."

doneWhen.en: Every box is assembled with brand marks on all visible sides and one finishing touch inside.
doneWhen.es: Every box is assembled with brand marks on all visible sides and one finishing touch inside.

watchFor.en: One decorated face and three blank ones. Turn the box over and ask what the customer sees from there.
watchFor.es: One decorated face and three blank ones. Turn the box over and ask what the customer sees from there.

description.en: Build or assemble box; Apply brand elements (logo, name, colors) to all sides; Add finishing touches (ribbon, seal, thank-you note inside); Quality check: does it look professional? Tier 1 (K-1): decorate a box that is already folded.
description.es: Build or assemble box; Apply brand elements (logo, name, colors) to all sides; Add finishing touches (ribbon, seal, thank-you note inside); Quality check: does it look professional? Tier 1 (K-1): decorate a box that is already folded.

sayThis.en: "Plain box, fifty cents. Your decoration, somewhere between a quarter and a dollar. Now write three prices: the thing on its own, the thing in a plain box, the thing in your box. Was the decoration worth what it cost?"
sayThis.es: "Plain box, fifty cents. Your decoration, somewhere between a quarter and a dollar. Now write three prices: the thing on its own, the thing in a plain box, the thing in your box. Was the decoration worth what it cost?"

doneWhen.en: Every sheet shows all three prices and a total packaging cost.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet shows all three prices and a total packaging cost.

watchFor.en: A dollar of decoration turning into five dollars of price with nobody asking who'd pay it. Ask.
watchFor.es: A dollar of decoration turning into five dollars of price with nobody asking who'd pay it. Ask.

description.en: Calculate packaging costs: plain box = $0.50, decoration supplies = $0.25-1.00 depending on use; Compare: product alone vs. in plain box vs. in branded box; Estimate: "What could I charge for each version?"; Discuss: packaging cost vs. increased perceived value—worth it? Tier 1 (K-1): say a price for the item in a plain box and in your box, and tell which is more.
description.es: Calculate packaging costs: plain box = $0.50, decoration supplies = $0.25-1.00 depending on use; Compare: product alone vs. in plain box vs. in branded box; Estimate: "What could I charge for each version?"; Discuss: packaging cost vs. increased perceived value—worth it? Tier 1 (K-1): say a price for the item in a plain box and in your box, and tell which is more.

sayThis.en: "One minute. Your customer, your brand, and why the box looks the way it does. Then the class answers one question — would you buy it?"
sayThis.es: "One minute. Your customer, your brand, and why the box looks the way it does. Then the class answers one question — would you buy it?"

doneWhen.en: Every presenter has taken a show-of-hands vote from the class.
doneWhen.es: Every presenter has taken a show-of-hands vote from the class.

watchFor.en: Pitches about how long it took to make. Nobody buys effort. Turn them back to the customer.
watchFor.es: Pitches about how long it took to make. Nobody buys effort. Turn them back to the customer.

description.en: 4-5 students present their packaged product to class (1 min each); Explain brand choices and target customer; Class feedback: would you buy it? Does packaging match product?
description.es: 4-5 students present their packaged product to class (1 min each); Explain brand choices and target customer; Class feedback: would you buy it? Does packaging match product?

discussionQuestions: "How did you choose your brand colors and design?"
"Does your packaging make the product look more valuable? How?"
"You spent $0.75 on packaging. Can you charge $2 more because of it? Why or why not?"
"What's the difference between cheap-looking and professional packaging?"
"How do real companies use packaging to sell products?"
"Can packaging be TOO fancy for a simple product? When does it not match?"
extensionIdeas: Create multiple packaging versions and price test with another class
Research real product packaging and analyze design choices
Design eco-friendly packaging (minimal materials but still attractive)
Create packaging "brand family" for multiple products
Photography session: product with and without packaging—compare appeal

beforeClass.en: Have the flat boxes ready to fold and the decoration scraps sorted. Make one example in advance: the same object in a plain box and in a branded box, side by side. That pair does most of the teaching for you.
beforeClass.es: Have the flat boxes ready to fold and the decoration scraps sorted. Make one example in advance: the same object in a plain box and in a branded box, side by side. That pair does most of the teaching for you.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: cut the pitch to three presenters. Short: add a second design of the same product aimed at a different customer.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: cut the pitch to three presenters. Short: add a second design of the same product aimed at a different customer.

Glue sticks, 8, covers this chapter and Chapter 11 — $5.00

Scrap paper for logo drafts before anyone draws on the box

Cost analysis worked on the board. The 50-cent box and the 25-cent to $1 decoration figures are lesson content, not purchases

Decoration scraps saved from earlier chapters — paper, fabric and ribbon ends — free

lowCost.description: Boxes and ribbon. The room already has the colour and the glue
items: Plain kraft boxes, 20 — $8.00

focus: Decorate pre-made bag or box (no assembly)
Draw simple pictures and colors
Focus on "making it pretty" vs. complex branding
Teacher helps with any writing

Simple box assembly or bag decoration
Can write brand name and draw simple logo
Choose colors with intention
Understand: decoration makes things look nicer

Assemble boxes with some precision
Design cohesive brand (name, logo, colors work together)
Can explain design choices

Complex box construction and design
