description.en: Explain market research: asking potential customers what they think before making product. Discuss: Why do businesses need to know what customers want? What questions should you ask? Introduce survey activity.
description.es: Explain market research: asking potential customers what they think before making product. Discuss: Why do businesses need to know what customers want? What questions should you ask? Introduce survey activity.

sayThis.en: "Before a business makes something, it asks people: would you buy this? That is called market research. Today you get to ask the questions."
sayThis.es: "Before a business makes something, it asks people: would you buy this? That is called market research. Today you get to ask the questions."

watchFor.en: Kids who think the maker should just decide. Ask what happens if you make twenty and nobody wants one.
watchFor.es: Kids who think the maker should just decide. Ask what happens if you make twenty and nobody wants one.

doneWhen.en: Two or three students have said why a business asks people first.
doneWhen.es: Two or three students have said why a business asks people first.

description.en: Students create 3-5 simple survey questions about a product (real or from class): Would you buy this? How much would you pay? What would make it better? What features matter most? Practice asking clearly. Tier 1 (K-1): use one yes/no question: "Would you buy this?"
description.es: Students create 3-5 simple survey questions about a product (real or from class): Would you buy this? How much would you pay? What would make it better? What features matter most? Practice asking clearly. Tier 1 (K-1): use one yes/no question: "Would you buy this?"

sayThis.en: "Write questions about your product. Start with: would you buy this? Then: how much would you pay? Read them to your partner to check they make sense."
sayThis.es: "Write questions about your product. Start with: would you buy this? Then: how much would you pay? Read them to your partner to check they make sense."

watchFor.en: Questions that push the answer, like "Don't you love it?" Rewrite one on the board as "Would you buy this?"
watchFor.es: Questions that push the answer, like "Don't you love it?" Rewrite one on the board as "Would you buy this?"

doneWhen.en: Every student has their questions written, and has read them to a partner.
doneWhen.es: Every student has their questions written, and has read them to a partner.

description.en: Students survey classmates about their product. Record responses: yes/no answers, price suggestions, feature preferences. Try to survey at least 5 people. Write down what they say. Tier 1 (K-1): ask the one yes/no question and make a tally mark for each answer.
description.es: Students survey classmates about their product. Record responses: yes/no answers, price suggestions, feature preferences. Try to survey at least 5 people. Write down what they say. Tier 1 (K-1): ask the one yes/no question and make a tally mark for each answer.

sayThis.en: "Ask five people. Use one pen color for yes and the other for no. Write down the price they say."
sayThis.es: "Ask five people. Use one pen color for yes and the other for no. Write down the price they say."

watchFor.en: Students asking only their best friend. Ask for two people they don't usually sit with.
watchFor.es: Students asking only their best friend. Ask for two people they don't usually sit with.

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has at least five answers on it.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has at least five answers on it.

description.en: Students organize survey results: How many would buy? What's the most common suggested price? What features do people want? Create simple chart or graph showing results. Tier 1 (K-1): count the yes and no tallies, and help build one class bar graph on the board.
description.es: Students organize survey results: How many would buy? What's the most common suggested price? What features do people want? Create simple chart or graph showing results. Tier 1 (K-1): count the yes and no tallies, and help build one class bar graph on the board.

sayThis.en: "Count your yes marks. Count your no marks. Which price did you hear most? Draw one bar for yes and one for no."
sayThis.es: "Count your yes marks. Count your no marks. Which price did you hear most? Draw one bar for yes and one for no."

watchFor.en: Messy tallies miscounted. Show how to count in bundles of five on the board.
watchFor.es: Messy tallies miscounted. Show how to count in bundles of five on the board.

doneWhen.en: Every student has a simple chart or graph showing their yes and no counts.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a simple chart or graph showing their yes and no counts.

description.en: Share survey results. Discuss: What did you learn? Were you surprised? Would you change your product based on feedback? Why is it important to ask customers before making something?
description.es: Share survey results. Discuss: What did you learn? Were you surprised? Would you change your product based on feedback? Why is it important to ask customers before making something?

sayThis.en: "Tell us one thing your survey told you. Would you change your product?"
sayThis.es: "Tell us one thing your survey told you. Would you change your product?"

watchFor.en: Answers like "people liked it." Ask for the number.
watchFor.es: Answers like "people liked it." Ask for the number.

doneWhen.en: At least three students have shared a number from their survey.
doneWhen.es: At least three students have shared a number from their survey.

discussionQuestions: Did everyone say yes? What does that tell you?
What if most people said no? Should you still make it?
How does asking first help you make smart choices?

beforeClass.en: Pick the product students will ask about — a class product or their own idea. Write one sample question on the board, like "Would you buy this?" Set out paper, the two-colour pens and a hardback book for each student to lean on.
beforeClass.es: Pick the product students will ask about — a class product or their own idea. Write one sample question on the board, like "Would you buy this?" Set out paper, the two-colour pens and a hardback book for each student to lean on.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: cut Survey Question Development to two questions and survey three people. Short: in Data Analysis, have each student add a title and labels to their graph.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: cut Survey Question Development to two questions and survey three people. Short: in Data Analysis, have each student add a title and labels to their graph.

30.label: 30 Minutes
30.bestFor: Standard class periods, weekly scheduling
materials: Clipboards or hard surface for writing
Chart paper or whiteboard for graphing

description.en: Each student chooses a product they want to "sell" (real or imaginary). Write it down with estimated price.
description.es: Each student chooses a product they want to "sell" (real or imaginary). Write it down with estimated price.

sayThis.en: "Pick one thing you would like to sell. It can be real or made up. Write its name and a price."
sayThis.es: "Pick one thing you would like to sell. It can be real or made up. Write its name and a price."

watchFor.en: Prices like a million dollars. Ask what they would pay for it themselves.
watchFor.es: Prices like a million dollars. Ask what they would pay for it themselves.

doneWhen.en: Every student has a product name and a price written down.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a product name and a price written down.

description.en: Create 3-question survey: "Would you buy this? How much would you pay? What features do you want?" Tier 1 (K-1): use one yes/no question: "Would you buy this?"
description.es: Create 3-question survey: "Would you buy this? How much would you pay? What features do you want?" Tier 1 (K-1): use one yes/no question: "Would you buy this?"

sayThis.en: "Write three questions at the top of your sheet. Would you buy this? How much would you pay? What features do you want?"
sayThis.es: "Write three questions at the top of your sheet. Would you buy this? How much would you pay? What features do you want?"

watchFor.en: Students adding words that push the answer, like "awesome." Keep the questions plain.
watchFor.es: Students adding words that push the answer, like "awesome." Keep the questions plain.

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has the three questions written at the top.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has the three questions written at the top.

description.en: Survey 8-10 classmates (or buddy class if available). Record answers carefully. Tier 1 (K-1): ask the one yes/no question and make a tally mark for each answer.
description.es: Survey 8-10 classmates (or buddy class if available). Record answers carefully. Tier 1 (K-1): ask the one yes/no question and make a tally mark for each answer.

sayThis.en: "Ask eight to ten people. Write each answer down right away. Yes in one color, no in the other."
sayThis.es: "Ask eight to ten people. Write each answer down right away. Yes in one color, no in the other."

watchFor.en: Students surveying the same few friends. Ask for at least three people they don't usually talk to.
watchFor.es: Students surveying the same few friends. Ask for at least three people they don't usually talk to.

doneWhen.en: Every sheet has at least eight answers recorded.
doneWhen.es: Every sheet has at least eight answers recorded.

description.en: Count answers. Create simple bar graph showing results (how many yes/no, price preferences). Tier 1 (K-1): count the yes and no tallies, and help build one class bar graph on the board.
description.es: Count answers. Create simple bar graph showing results (how many yes/no, price preferences). Tier 1 (K-1): count the yes and no tallies, and help build one class bar graph on the board.

sayThis.en: "Count the yes and the no. Draw one bar for each. Make each bar as tall as its number. Then do the same for the prices."
sayThis.es: "Count the yes and the no. Draw one bar for each. Make each bar as tall as its number. Then do the same for the prices."

watchFor.en: Bars drawn by guess. Draw one on the board first, counting up the squares out loud.
watchFor.es: Bars drawn by guess. Draw one on the board first, counting up the squares out loud.

doneWhen.en: Every student has a bar graph with labeled yes and no bars.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a bar graph with labeled yes and no bars.

description.en: "Based on your data, should you make this product? What changes should you make?"
description.es: "Based on your data, should you make this product? What changes should you make?"

sayThis.en: "Look at your graph. Should you make this product? What one thing would you change?"
sayThis.es: "Look at your graph. Should you make this product? What one thing would you change?"

watchFor.en: Students ignoring a tall no bar. Ask what the biggest bar is telling them.
watchFor.es: Students ignoring a tall no bar. Ask what the biggest bar is telling them.

doneWhen.en: Every student has said or written a yes or no decision and one change.
doneWhen.es: Every student has said or written a yes or no decision and one change.

description.en: Partner share: "What did your research tell you?"
description.es: Partner share: "What did your research tell you?"

sayThis.en: "Tell your partner: my research told me ___."
sayThis.es: "Tell your partner: my research told me ___."

watchFor.en: Pairs drifting off topic. Give the sentence start and call time at one minute.
watchFor.es: Pairs drifting off topic. Give the sentence start and call time at one minute.

doneWhen.en: Every pair has finished the sentence out loud.
doneWhen.es: Every pair has finished the sentence out loud.

discussionQuestions: Did anyone's data surprise them?
What's the most popular price range?
Did anyone decide NOT to make their product after the survey? Why?
How is research different from guessing?
What if you skipped research and made 100 products nobody wanted?
extensionIdeas: Create a class "Market Research Report" poster showing all findings.

beforeClass.en: Decide who students may survey — classmates, or a buddy class if you can — and warn that teacher. Write the three survey questions on the board. Set out paper, the two-colour pens and a book to lean on.
beforeClass.es: Decide who students may survey — classmates, or a buddy class if you can — and warn that teacher. Write the three survey questions on the board. Set out paper, the two-colour pens and a book to lean on.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: survey five classmates instead of eight to ten. Short: in Analysis & Decision, have each student write one change and the number from the data that made them choose it.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: survey five classmates instead of eight to ten. Short: in Analysis & Decision, have each student write one change and the number from the data that made them choose it.

45.label: 45 Minutes
materials: Graph paper or printed graph templates
Optional: access to another class for broader survey base

sayThis.en: "Design something and put a price on it. Then write your guess: out of ten people, how many say yes? Write the number now, because at the end you'll want to claim you knew all along."
sayThis.es: "Design something and put a price on it. Then write your guess: out of ten people, how many say yes? Write the number now, because at the end you'll want to claim you knew all along."

doneWhen.en: Every student has a sketch, a name, a price and a written prediction.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a sketch, a name, a price and a written prediction.

watchFor.en: Guesses of ten out of ten. Let them stand. The data does the arguing later.
watchFor.es: Guesses of ten out of ten. Let them stand. The data does the arguing later.

description.en: Each student designs a product (sketch + name + description + initial price) Write "hypothesis": "I think [number] out of 10 people will want to buy this"
description.es: Each student designs a product (sketch + name + description + initial price) Write "hypothesis": "I think [number] out of 10 people will want to buy this"

sayThis.en: "Five to seven questions. Ask what they'd pay, not whether they like it — liking it is free. Then test your questions on your partner. If they ask what you mean, the question is broken."
sayThis.es: "Five to seven questions. Ask what they'd pay, not whether they like it — liking it is free. Then test your questions on your partner. If they ask what you mean, the question is broken."

doneWhen.en: Every survey has at least five questions tested on a partner.
doneWhen.es: Every survey has at least five questions tested on a partner.

watchFor.en: Questions that lead the answer. "Don't you think this is great?" Rewrite one in front of the class.
watchFor.es: Questions that lead the answer. "Don't you think this is great?" Rewrite one in front of the class.

description.en: Design 5-7 questions: Would you buy? Price range? Preferred features/colors? What problems does it solve? What would make it better? Test questions on partner for clarity. Tier 1 (K-1): use one yes/no question: "Would you buy this?"
description.es: Design 5-7 questions: Would you buy? Price range? Preferred features/colors? What problems does it solve? What would make it better? Test questions on partner for clarity. Tier 1 (K-1): use one yes/no question: "Would you buy this?"

sayThis.en: "Ten to fifteen people. Write every answer down as you get it, including the rude ones. Especially the rude ones. Those are the useful ones."
sayThis.es: "Ten to fifteen people. Write every answer down as you get it, including the rude ones. Especially the rude ones. Those are the useful ones."

doneWhen.en: Every data sheet has at least ten responses recorded.
doneWhen.es: Every data sheet has at least ten responses recorded.

watchFor.en: Students surveying only their friends. Set a rule: at least five people you don't usually talk to.
watchFor.es: Students surveying only their friends. Set a rule: at least five people you don't usually talk to.

description.en: Survey 10-15 people (classmates, another class, or school staff) Record all answers on data sheets Note unexpected feedback or suggestions. Tier 1 (K-1): ask the one yes/no question and make a tally mark for each answer.
description.es: Survey 10-15 people (classmates, another class, or school staff) Record all answers on data sheets Note unexpected feedback or suggestions. Tier 1 (K-1): ask the one yes/no question and make a tally mark for each answer.

sayThis.en: "Tally it. Turn it into a bar chart. Work out the percentage. Then write your prediction next to the real number and look at the gap."
sayThis.es: "Tally it. Turn it into a bar chart. Work out the percentage. Then write your prediction next to the real number and look at the gap."

doneWhen.en: Every student has a bar graph with their prediction written beside the actual result.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a bar graph with their prediction written beside the actual result.

watchFor.en: Percentages done by feel. Work one out on the board with the whole room first.
watchFor.es: Percentages done by feel. Work one out on the board with the whole room first.

description.en: Tally all responses Create bar graphs showing: interest level, price preferences, feature preferences Calculate percentages (e.g., "60% said yes, 40% said no") Compare hypothesis to actual results. Tier 1 (K-1): count the yes and no tallies and say which is more — no percentages.
description.es: Tally all responses Create bar graphs showing: interest level, price preferences, feature preferences Calculate percentages (e.g., "60% said yes, 40% said no") Compare hypothesis to actual results. Tier 1 (K-1): count the yes and no tallies and say which is more — no percentages.

sayThis.en: "Change one thing because of the data, not because you felt like it. The price, a feature, or who it's for. Then write down what the data said that made you change it."
sayThis.es: "Change one thing because of the data, not because you felt like it. The price, a feature, or who it's for. Then write down what the data said that made you change it."

doneWhen.en: Every product shows a before and an after with the reason written between them.
doneWhen.es: Every product shows a before and an after with the reason written between them.

watchFor.en: Students refusing to change anything. Ask what their lowest-scoring answer was and start there.
watchFor.es: Students refusing to change anything. Ask what their lowest-scoring answer was and start there.

description.en: Based on data, adjust product: change price, add/remove features, change target customer Create "before and after" comparison showing changes made
description.es: Based on data, adjust product: change price, add/remove features, change target customer Create "before and after" comparison showing changes made

sayThis.en: "One page. The idea, the graph, what you found out, what you changed. That's a real report. Businesses pay a lot of money for that page."
sayThis.es: "One page. The idea, the graph, what you found out, what you changed. That's a real report. Businesses pay a lot of money for that page."

doneWhen.en: Every report page has all four parts filled in.
doneWhen.es: Every report page has all four parts filled in.

watchFor.en: Pages with a graph and no findings. The sentence under the graph is the report.
watchFor.es: Pages with a graph and no findings. The sentence under the graph is the report.

description.en: Complete one-page report: Product idea, survey results (graphs), key findings, product changes made based on feedback. Tier 1 (K-1): say the result out loud, like "5 said yes, 3 said no."
description.es: Complete one-page report: Product idea, survey results (graphs), key findings, product changes made based on feedback. Tier 1 (K-1): say the result out loud, like "5 said yes, 3 said no."

discussionQuestions: How many people's hypothesis was wrong? What does that teach us?

If 8 out of 10 people want blue but you only make red, what happens?

What's the difference between making what YOU like vs. what CUSTOMERS want?
extensionIdeas: Survey a second group and compare results (do different groups want different things?)
Calculate potential profit: "If 60% of 100 people buy at $5, and it costs $2 to make, what's your profit?"
Research real market research examples (taste tests, focus groups, beta testing)
Create survey for school cafeteria or library to improve services
Design a "bad survey" with confusing questions, then redesign it properly

beforeClass.en: Arrange in advance who the students may survey — another class, the office, the kitchen — and warn those adults it's coming. A survey with nobody to ask collapses halfway through the lesson.
beforeClass.es: Arrange in advance who the students may survey — another class, the office, the kitchen — and warn those adults it's coming. A survey with nobody to ask collapses halfway through the lesson.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: cut the report to the graph and three bullet points. Short: add a second survey round after the product is adjusted.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: cut the report to the graph and three bullet points. Short: add a second survey round after the product is adjusted.

title.en: Production Day: Build Your Product for Real
title.es: Production Day: Build Your Product for Real

materials: Simple craft materials (paper, cardboard, tape, scissors)

description.es: Review product plans from earlier lessons. Explain production goal: make your actual product today. Gather all materials needed. Set quality standards: careful work, attention to detail.

sayThis.es: "Today you make your product for real. Look at your plan. Get what you need. Work slow and neat — careful work is good work."

watchFor.en: Kids with no plan. Hand them the template and let them start.
watchFor.es: Kids with no plan. Hand them the template and let them start.

doneWhen.en: Every student has a plan or template and their materials on the desk.
doneWhen.es: Every student has a plan or template and their materials on the desk.

description.es: Students build their planned products using materials collected. Follow blueprints or plans. Work carefully and thoughtfully. Ask for help if stuck. Focus on quality craftsmanship.

sayThis.es: "Build it the way your plan shows. Stuck? Try one more time, then put your hand up."

doneWhen.es: Every student has a built product that matches the plan.

sayThis.es: "Now you are the checker. Does it look like your plan? Is it strong? Does it work? Find one thing to fix and fix it."

doneWhen.es: Every student has fixed at least one thing on their product.

description.es: Students build their products following their blueprints. Work through production steps methodically. Measure carefully, assemble thoughtfully, join pieces securely. Troubleshoot problems as they arise. Maintain focus on quality throughout production.

sayThis.en: "Follow your blueprint step by step. Measure before you cut. Join pieces so they hold. If something goes wrong, fix it and keep going."
sayThis.es: "Follow your blueprint step by step. Measure before you cut. Join pieces so they hold. If something goes wrong, fix it and keep going."

watchFor.en: Cutting before measuring. Ask to see the ruler mark before the scissors come out.
watchFor.es: Cutting before measuring. Ask to see the ruler mark before the scissors come out.

doneWhen.en: Every student has an assembled product.
doneWhen.es: Every student has an assembled product.

description.en: Students conduct thorough quality checks: structural integrity, appearance, functionality. Make refinements: sand rough edges, secure loose parts, add protective coating if applicable. Add final details: labels, decorations, packaging if designed. No sandpaper or coating? Trim rough edges with scissors and cover them with tape.
description.es: Students conduct thorough quality checks: structural integrity, appearance, functionality. Make refinements: sand rough edges, secure loose parts, add protective coating if applicable. Add final details: labels, decorations, packaging if designed. No sandpaper or coating? Trim rough edges with scissors and cover them with tape.

sayThis.en: "Check it three ways. Is it strong? Does it look good? Does it work? Fix whatever fails. Then add labels and decorations."
sayThis.es: "Check it three ways. Is it strong? Does it look good? Does it work? Fix whatever fails. Then add labels and decorations."

watchFor.en: Decorating before fixing. Weak spots first, decorations last.
watchFor.es: Decorating before fixing. Weak spots first, decorations last.

doneWhen.en: Every product has passed all three checks and has its finishing details.
doneWhen.es: Every product has passed all three checks and has its finishing details.

description.en: Students present finished products: demonstrate features, explain production process, discuss challenges overcome. Class provides feedback. Reflect: What went well? What would you do differently? How does your product match your original vision? What did you learn about production?
description.es: Students present finished products: demonstrate features, explain production process, discuss challenges overcome. Class provides feedback. Reflect: What went well? What would you do differently? How does your product match your original vision? What did you learn about production?

sayThis.en: "Show your product. Tell us one thing that went well and one thing you would do differently next time."
sayThis.es: "Show your product. Tell us one thing that went well and one thing you would do differently next time."

watchFor.en: Only the confident students sharing. Have partners share first, then pick two for the class.
watchFor.es: Only the confident students sharing. Have partners share first, then pick two for the class.

doneWhen.en: Every student has said one thing that went well and one thing to change.
doneWhen.es: Every student has said one thing that went well and one thing to change.

discussionQuestions: Did planning your steps first help or make it harder?
Which step was hardest? Which was fastest?
How did you decide if quality was good enough?
Did your time goal help you finish?
What would you change if you did this again?

beforeClass.en: Put each student's blueprint and materials list on their desk, with the template ready for anyone without one. Set paper, cardboard, scissors, glue, tape, rulers and markers in one supply area.
beforeClass.es: Put each student's blueprint and materials list on their desk, with the template ready for anyone without one. Set paper, cardboard, scissors, glue, tape, rulers and markers in one supply area.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: turn Product Showcase & Reflection into a quiet gallery walk with products on desks. Short: in Quality Assurance & Finishing, add a label or packaging to each product.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: turn Product Showcase & Reflection into a quiet gallery walk with products on desks. Short: in Quality Assurance & Finishing, add a label or packaging to each product.

45.label: 45 Minutes
45.activityName: Complete Production Workshop with Cost & Quality Analysis
materials: Multiple craft material options with posted "costs" (cardboard = 10¢, tape = 5¢, marker use = 2¢, etc.)
Materials budget written at the top of each group's plan sheet — the Materials Manager subtracts every purchase
Production role badges (Designer, Builder, Quality Inspector, Materials Manager)

sayThis.en: "Four jobs. Designer keeps it matching the plan. Builder builds. Inspector says yes or no. Materials Manager holds the money. One job each. Then guess two numbers: how many can you make, and how long will each one take?"
sayThis.es: "Four jobs. Designer keeps it matching the plan. Builder builds. Inspector says yes or no. Materials Manager holds the money. One job each. Then guess two numbers: how many can you make, and how long will each one take?"

doneWhen.en: Every group has four named roles and a written estimate of quantity and time.
doneWhen.es: Every group has four named roles and a written estimate of quantity and time.

watchFor.en: Groups where the Builder quietly does everything. Name the four jobs out loud and have each person say theirs back.
watchFor.es: Groups where the Builder quietly does everything. Name the four jobs out loud and have each person say theirs back.

description.en: Groups choose product to make (from blueprints created in CH9, or teacher-provided options) Assign production roles (Designer, Builder, Quality Inspector, Materials Manager) Estimate: How many can we make? How long will each take? What will materials cost? Write production plan with goals
description.es: Groups choose product to make (from blueprints created in CH9, or teacher-provided options) Assign production roles (Designer, Builder, Quality Inspector, Materials Manager) Estimate: How many can we make? How long will each take? What will materials cost? Write production plan with goals

sayThis.en: "Write your budget at the top of the sheet. Materials Manager buys, and writes down what everything cost. When the budget's gone, production stops."
sayThis.es: "Write your budget at the top of the sheet. Materials Manager buys, and writes down what everything cost. When the budget's gone, production stops."

doneWhen.en: Every group has a budget written down and a purchase list with prices.
doneWhen.es: Every group has a budget written down and a purchase list with prices.

watchFor.en: Groups buying everything in the first ten seconds. Ask what they'll do when a piece gets ruined.
watchFor.es: Groups buying everything in the first ten seconds. Ask what they'll do when a piece gets ruined.

description.en: Each group writes a $5-10 materials budget at the top of its plan sheet Materials Manager "purchases" materials needed (tracking costs) Calculate estimated cost per item. Tier 1 (K-1): pick materials from the shop and count what they cost together, up to $10.
description.es: Each group writes a $5-10 materials budget at the top of its plan sheet Materials Manager "purchases" materials needed (tracking costs) Calculate estimated cost per item. Tier 1 (K-1): pick materials from the shop and count what they cost together, up to $10.

sayThis.en: "Timer's running. Build to the plan, not to what you feel like doing. Inspector, check each one as it's finished, not at the end. Materials Manager, keep writing."
sayThis.es: "Timer's running. Build to the plan, not to what you feel like doing. Inspector, check each one as it's finished, not at the end. Materials Manager, keep writing."

doneWhen.en: Every group has finished items, a materials tally and a time per item.
doneWhen.es: Every group has finished items, a materials tally and a time per item.

watchFor.en: The Inspector waving everything through. Ask them to reject one and say why.
watchFor.es: The Inspector waving everything through. Ask them to reject one and say why.

description.en: Build items according to plan Designer ensures items match blueprint Builder assembles Quality Inspector checks each finished piece against rubric Materials Manager tracks supply use Timer running — track time per item
description.es: Build items according to plan Designer ensures items match blueprint Builder assembles Quality Inspector checks each finished piece against rubric Materials Manager tracks supply use Timer running — track time per item

sayThis.en: "Two piles. Approved, and needs work. Inspector says which and says why. Nobody takes it personally — that's the job."
sayThis.es: "Two piles. Approved, and needs work. Inspector says which and says why. Nobody takes it personally — that's the job."

doneWhen.en: Every group's items are sorted into two counted piles.
doneWhen.es: Every group's items are sorted into two counted piles.

watchFor.en: Groups approving all of their own. Have one group inspect another group's pile.
watchFor.es: Groups approving all of their own. Have one group inspect another group's pile.

description.en: Quality Inspector presents finished items Class reviews: Does it match the plan? Is quality good? Would customers buy this? Separate "approved" vs. "needs improvement" items
description.es: Quality Inspector presents finished items Class reviews: Does it match the plan? Is quality good? Would customers buy this? Separate "approved" vs. "needs improvement" items

sayThis.en: "You planned ten and made eight. You said ninety seconds and it took two minutes. That isn't failure — every factory finds this out. Now: cost per item is money spent divided by items approved. The rejects still cost you."
sayThis.es: "You planned ten and made eight. You said ninety seconds and it took two minutes. That isn't failure — every factory finds this out. Now: cost per item is money spent divided by items approved. The rejects still cost you."

doneWhen.en: Every Production Report shows planned against actual for both count and time, plus a cost per approved item.
doneWhen.es: Every Production Report shows planned against actual for both count and time, plus a cost per approved item.

watchFor.en: Dividing by everything made instead of everything approved. That difference is the whole lesson about waste.
watchFor.es: Dividing by everything made instead of everything approved. That difference is the whole lesson about waste.

description.en: Calculate actual vs. estimated production (made 8, planned 10) Calculate actual vs. estimated time (took 2 min each, estimated 1.5 min) Calculate actual cost per item (materials used ÷ items approved) Calculate "waste rate" if materials were rejected Complete Production Report form. Tier 1 (K-1): count how many you made and how many passed, and say which pile is bigger.
description.es: Calculate actual vs. estimated production (made 8, planned 10) Calculate actual vs. estimated time (took 2 min each, estimated 1.5 min) Calculate actual cost per item (materials used ÷ items approved) Calculate "waste rate" if materials were rejected Complete Production Report form. Tier 1 (K-1): count how many you made and how many passed, and say which pile is bigger.

discussionQuestions: How did your actual production compare to your estimate?
What took longer than expected? Why?
Did quality go up or down as you got faster?
Which role was most important to success?
How did division of labor help your team?
What cost more than expected? What cost less?
If you were making 100 of these, what would you change?
How is this like the friends' experience in the workshop?
extensionIdeas: Round 2 production: "Now make 5 more. Will you be faster? Track improvement."
Cost comparison: "Store version costs $3. Your version costs 75¢ in materials. What about your time?"
Gallery display with "Made by [Team Name]" signs and production stats cards
Calculate profit if sold at market (Price - Cost = Profit per item)
Create "Lessons Learned" poster for future production runs

beforeClass.en: Pull the Chapter 9 blueprints out and put them on the desks, plus two options of your own for groups whose plans went missing. Set the materials out like a shop, with the prices showing.
beforeClass.es: Pull the Chapter 9 blueprints out and put them on the desks, plus two options of your own for groups whose plans went missing. Set the materials out like a shop, with the prices showing.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: cut the quality review to the inspector's verdict only. Short: add a second production run using what they learned in the first.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: cut the quality review to the inspector's verdict only. Short: add a second production run using what they learned in the first.

standard.label: From Scratch
standard.description: One pack of construction paper. The template is photocopied for students without a blueprint
items: Construction paper, 1 assorted pack of 100 sheets — $5.00. The finished products need to look different from each other
One teacher-made product template, photocopied, one per student
Two boxes labelled "passed" and "needs work" — free, use delivery boxes
Timer or classroom clock for the production round, visible to the whole class
Paper, pencils and glue sticks from the Chapter 1 and Chapter 4 restock
Scissors from the Season 1 kit
Recycled cardboard from delivery boxes — free, ask the office
Masking tape from the Chapter 3 restock
Markers from the Chapter 1 and Chapter 4 restock
Rulers from the Season 1 kit, for measuring before cutting
Each group's Chapter 9 blueprint, from the student folders
A shop price sign for the materials, role badges and the Production Report, all handwritten on paper — free

lowCost.label: Basic Classroom
lowCost.description: One pack of construction paper. Everything else is in the room
items: Construction paper, 1 assorted pack of 100 sheets — $5.00
One teacher-made product template, photocopied, one per student
Two boxes labelled "passed" and "needs work" — free, use delivery boxes
Timer or classroom clock, visible to the whole class
Paper, pencils, scissors and glue sticks from the classroom supply
Recycled cardboard from delivery boxes — free
Masking tape, markers and rulers from the classroom supply
Chapter 9 blueprints, from the student folders
Shop price sign, role badges and Production Report handwritten on paper — free

focus: Make one simple item together as whole class first
Focus on following steps and finishing
Quality = "Did you finish it? Is it neat?"
Celebrate completion, not speed
Basic vocabulary: make, build, finish, good, done
Partner production with role assignment (one cuts, one decorates)
Simple quality checklist (neat? complete? sturdy?)
Track total made and time taken
Vocabulary: production, quality, teamwork, finished
Small groups with assigned roles
Track materials used vs. planned
Quality rubric with 3 criteria
Calculate simple costs (items made × cost per item)
Vocabulary: production plan, quality control, materials cost, efficiency
Full production simulation with budgeting
Multiple roles with clear responsibilities
Detailed time and cost tracking
Quality control with accept/reject decisions and waste calculation
Advanced vocabulary: production rate, cost per unit, quality standards, division of labor, waste percentage, profit margin

ell.label: English Language Learners
strategies: Show each build step once before students start, pointing to the matching part of the plan.
In the 45-minute version, give role badges a picture: a pencil for Designer, a hammer for Builder.
Pair students with a partner who can repeat directions.

learningDifferences.label: Students with Learning Differences
strategies: Break the build into short numbered steps and check off each one.
Keep a finished example on the desk for students to match.
Offer the simpler photocopied template to a student overwhelmed by their own blueprint.

advanced.label: Advanced Students
strategies: Time each build step and suggest one change that would make production faster.
Work out the cost per item for their product using the posted material prices.
Plan a second production run and predict how many more items they could make.

title.en: Our Makers' Faire: Season Showcase & Sale
title.es: Our Makers' Faire: Season Showcase & Sale

20.label: 20 Minutes
20.bestFor: Tight schedules, daily scheduling
materials: Student-made items from earlier in the season (or simple items made just for this activity)
Paper clips as $1 tokens, 50 per shopper — reused every year

description.en: Explain Makers' Faire concept: showcase student-made products, demonstrate making skills, celebrate creativity. Students will display products and share making stories. Review faire setup and expectations.
description.es: Explain Makers' Faire concept: showcase student-made products, demonstrate making skills, celebrate creativity. Students will display products and share making stories. Review faire setup and expectations.

sayThis.en: "Today is our Makers' Faire. You show what you made and tell how you made it. First you set up a booth. Then you take turns being the maker and the visitor."
sayThis.es: "Today is our Makers' Faire. You show what you made and tell how you made it. First you set up a booth. Then you take turns being the maker and the visitor."

watchFor.en: Kids worried nobody will like their item. Tell them every booth gets visitors.
watchFor.es: Kids worried nobody will like their item. Tell them every booth gets visitors.

doneWhen.en: Every student knows which desk is their booth.
doneWhen.es: Every student knows which desk is their booth.

description.en: Students create display booths for their products: arrange items attractively, create signs with product names and prices, make labels explaining what they made and how. Organize workspace to demonstrate making process if applicable.
description.es: Students create display booths for their products: arrange items attractively, create signs with product names and prices, make labels explaining what they made and how. Organize workspace to demonstrate making process if applicable.

sayThis.en: "Make your booth. Put your things out nicely. Make a sign with the name and the price. Make a card that says what you made and how."
sayThis.es: "Make your booth. Put your things out nicely. Make a sign with the name and the price. Make a card that says what you made and how."

watchFor.en: Signs too small to read. Hold one up across the room and ask if they can read it.
watchFor.es: Signs too small to read. Hold one up across the room and ask if they can read it.

doneWhen.en: Every booth has items out, a sign and a label.
doneWhen.es: Every booth has items out, a sign and a label.

description.en: Run the faire! Students take turns being booth vendors (presenting their work) and faire visitors (viewing others' work). Vendors explain their products, making process, and what they learned. Visitors ask questions and appreciate creativity.
description.es: Run the faire! Students take turns being booth vendors (presenting their work) and faire visitors (viewing others' work). Vendors explain their products, making process, and what they learned. Visitors ask questions and appreciate creativity.

sayThis.en: "Makers, stand at your booth and tell visitors how you made it. Visitors, ask one question at each booth. When I clap, switch."
sayThis.es: "Makers, stand at your booth and tell visitors how you made it. Visitors, ask one question at each booth. When I clap, switch."

watchFor.en: Visitors crowding one booth. Send twos and threes to the empty booths.
watchFor.es: Visitors crowding one booth. Send twos and threes to the empty booths.

doneWhen.en: Every student has been both a maker and a visitor.
doneWhen.es: Every student has been both a maker and a visitor.

description.en: Gather for closing circle. Celebrate accomplishments: what were you most proud of making? What was the biggest challenge you overcame? What did you learn about being a maker? How does making things yourself feel different from buying things?
description.es: Gather for closing circle. Celebrate accomplishments: what were you most proud of making? What was the biggest challenge you overcame? What did you learn about being a maker? How does making things yourself feel different from buying things?

sayThis.en: "Come to the circle. What are you most proud of making? How is making something different from buying it?"
sayThis.es: "Come to the circle. What are you most proud of making? How is making something different from buying it?"

watchFor.en: Everyone repeating the last answer. Ask for one nobody has said yet.
watchFor.es: Everyone repeating the last answer. Ask for one nobody has said yet.

doneWhen.en: Every student has shared one thing they are proud of.
doneWhen.es: Every student has shared one thing they are proud of.

discussionQuestions: Did visitors like your items? How did it feel to show them?
What did you learn about sharing your work with others?
What was your favorite thing you made this season?

beforeClass.en: Have each student's finished items from earlier Season 3 chapters ready on their desk. Put cardstock, paper and markers out for signs and labels. Decide where the booths go so visitors can walk between them.
beforeClass.es: Have each student's finished items from earlier Season 3 chapters ready on their desk. Put cardstock, paper and markers out for signs and labels. Decide where the booths go so visitors can walk between them.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: cut Booth Setup & Organization to one sign and one label per booth. Short: in Makers' Faire Presentation, add a second switch so every student visits more booths.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: cut Booth Setup & Organization to one sign and one label per booth. Short: in Makers' Faire Presentation, add a second switch so every student visits more booths.

30.label: 30 Minutes
30.bestFor: Standard class periods, weekly scheduling
30.activityName: Classroom Makers' Faire with Sales Tracking
materials: Student-made items from the season (pottery, inventions, blueprints, decorated boxes, etc.)
Index cards for price tags and "About This Product" cards
Paper clips as $1 tokens, 50 per shopper — reused every year
Simple sales tracking sheet (tally marks or numbers)
Display materials (fabric scraps, small boxes for height variation)

description.en: Students arrange items on desk with price tags and product description cards ("I made this [item]. It is made from [materials]. It took [time].")
description.es: Students arrange items on desk with price tags and product description cards ("I made this [item]. It is made from [materials]. It took [time].")

sayThis.en: "Put your things on your desk. Every item needs a price tag. Then fill in a card: I made this ___. It is made from ___. It took ___."
sayThis.es: "Put your things on your desk. Every item needs a price tag. Then fill in a card: I made this ___. It is made from ___. It took ___."

watchFor.en: Prices too high to sell. Remind them each shopper has only 50 tokens for the whole faire.
watchFor.es: Prices too high to sell. Remind them each shopper has only 50 tokens for the whole faire.

doneWhen.en: Every item has a price tag and every booth has a product card.
doneWhen.es: Every item has a price tag and every booth has a product card.

description.en: Everyone walks around viewing all booths before shopping opens. Mental note of favorites.
description.es: Everyone walks around viewing all booths before shopping opens. Mental note of favorites.

sayThis.en: "Walk and look. No buying yet. Pick two things you want to come back for."
sayThis.es: "Walk and look. No buying yet. Pick two things you want to come back for."

watchFor.en: Kids trying to buy now. Hands in pockets until the round starts.
watchFor.es: Kids trying to buy now. Hands in pockets until the round starts.

doneWhen.en: Everyone has passed every booth and is back at their place.
doneWhen.es: Everyone has passed every booth and is back at their place.

description.en: Half the class shops with 50 tokens, each worth $1. Make purchasing decisions, practice counting change, track sales. Tier 1 (K-1): pay one token for each dollar on the tag.
description.es: Half the class shops with 50 tokens, each worth $1. Make purchasing decisions, practice counting change, track sales. Tier 1 (K-1): pay one token for each dollar on the tag.

sayThis.en: "Shoppers, you have 50 tokens. Each one is one dollar. Pay the number on the tag. Sellers, make a tally mark for every sale."
sayThis.es: "Shoppers, you have 50 tokens. Each one is one dollar. Pay the number on the tag. Sellers, make a tally mark for every sale."

watchFor.en: Sales with no tally mark. Stop at halfway and have every seller check their sheet.
watchFor.es: Sales with no tally mark. Stop at halfway and have every seller check their sheet.

doneWhen.en: Every seller has tally marks and every shopper has spent or chosen to keep their tokens.
doneWhen.es: Every seller has tally marks and every shopper has spent or chosen to keep their tokens.

description.en: Shoppers become sellers, sellers become shoppers. Continue faire.
description.es: Shoppers become sellers, sellers become shoppers. Continue faire.

sayThis.en: "Sellers, count your tokens and write the number on your sheet. Now swap. Shoppers, give me your leftover tokens and go run a booth."
sayThis.es: "Sellers, count your tokens and write the number on your sheet. Now swap. Shoppers, give me your leftover tokens and go run a booth."

watchFor.en: New shoppers holding fewer than 50 tokens. Top each one up to 50 from the leftover pile before they shop.
watchFor.es: New shoppers holding fewer than 50 tokens. Top each one up to 50 from the leftover pile before they shop.

doneWhen.en: Every Round 1 seller has a token count written down and Round 2 sales are being tallied.
doneWhen.es: Every Round 1 seller has a token count written down and Round 2 sales are being tallied.

description.en: Count the tokens collected. If using costs: subtract material costs (from earlier activities) to find profit. Tier 1 (K-1): count tokens in piles of ten and skip the costs.
description.es: Count the tokens collected. If using costs: subtract material costs (from earlier activities) to find profit. Tier 1 (K-1): count tokens in piles of ten and skip the costs.

sayThis.en: "Count your tokens in piles of ten. Each token is one dollar. Write your total. If you know what your materials cost, take that away — that is your profit."
sayThis.es: "Count your tokens in piles of ten. Each token is one dollar. Write your total. If you know what your materials cost, take that away — that is your profit."

watchFor.en: Tokens counted one at a time and lost track of. Piles of ten on the desk, then count the piles.
watchFor.es: Tokens counted one at a time and lost track of. Piles of ten on the desk, then count the piles.

doneWhen.en: Every seller has a dollar total written on their sheet.
doneWhen.es: Every seller has a dollar total written on their sheet.

description.en: Share: "I earned $___. The best part of the Makers' Faire was ___."
description.es: Share: "I earned $___. The best part of the Makers' Faire was ___."

sayThis.en: "Finish this: I earned ___ dollars. The best part of the Makers' Faire was ___."
sayThis.es: "Finish this: I earned ___ dollars. The best part of the Makers' Faire was ___."

watchFor.en: Long answers that run over. One sentence each, and keep it moving.
watchFor.es: Long answers that run over. One sentence each, and keep it moving.

doneWhen.en: Every student has filled both blanks out loud.
doneWhen.es: Every student has filled both blanks out loud.

discussionQuestions: What sold the fastest? Why do you think?
How did you decide what to buy when you were shopping?
Which product took the most work to make? Did it cost more?
What was the hardest part of running your booth?
What did you learn from this whole season?
extensionIdeas: Create a class "Makers' Faire Report" with photos of booths, total items sold, and favorite moments.

beforeClass.en: Count the paper clips into bundles of 50 — each clip is a $1 token, and a box of 500 covers ten shoppers. Put paper, markers and a tally sheet at each booth, and pick which half of the class shops first. Round 2 shoppers reuse the same 500 tokens.
beforeClass.es: Count the paper clips into bundles of 50 — each clip is a $1 token, and a box of 500 covers ten shoppers. Put paper, markers and a tally sheet at each booth, and pick which half of the class shops first. Round 2 shoppers reuse the same 500 tokens.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: skip the Gallery Preview Walk and go straight to Shopping Round 1. Short: add a clearance round at the end where unsold items get a lower price.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: skip the Gallery Preview Walk and go straight to Shopping Round 1. Short: add a clearance round at the end where unsold items get a lower price.

45.label: 45 Minutes
45.activityName: Full Makers' Faire with Business Reporting and Season Celebration
materials: Complete collection of student-made items from S3 chapters (pottery, woodworking projects, inventions, blueprints, decorated items, prototypes)
Professional-looking price tags (printed or nicely handwritten)
"Product Story" cards (name, materials, time to make, inspiration, skills learned)
Paper clips as $10 tokens, 10-15 per shopper — reused every year
Display materials (fabric, risers, booth signs, string lights optional)

sayThis.en: "Your booth needs four things. A sign with your name. A price on everything. A story card saying how you made it and what you learned. And somewhere to keep the money. Prices come from what it cost you plus your time — not from what you wish it was worth."
sayThis.es: "Your booth needs four things. A sign with your name. A price on everything. A story card saying how you made it and what you learned. And somewhere to keep the money. Prices come from what it cost you plus your time — not from what you wish it was worth."

doneWhen.en: Every booth has a sign, priced items, a story card and a cash area.
doneWhen.es: Every booth has a sign, priced items, a story card and a cash area.

watchFor.en: Everything laid flat on the desk. Stack a book under one item and show them what height does.
watchFor.es: Everything laid flat on the desk. Stack a book under one item and show them what height does.

description.en: Arrange multiple items with attractive display (height variation, visual appeal) Create booth sign with student/team name: "[Name]'s Makers' Booth" Set up price tags based on actual material costs + time/skill value Display "Product Story" cards explaining the creation process and skills used Arrange sales log and "cashbox" area. Tier 1 (K-1): price each item in whole tokens, like 1, 2 or 3 tokens.
description.es: Arrange multiple items with attractive display (height variation, visual appeal) Create booth sign with student/team name: "[Name]'s Makers' Booth" Set up price tags based on actual material costs + time/skill value Display "Product Story" cards explaining the creation process and skills used Arrange sales log and "cashbox" area. Tier 1 (K-1): price each item in whole tokens, like 1, 2 or 3 tokens.

sayThis.en: "Two rules. Walk the whole room before you buy anything. And every seller says thank you, whether they sell or not. Ribbon's cut. The faire is open."
sayThis.es: "Two rules. Walk the whole room before you buy anything. And every seller says thank you, whether they sell or not. Ribbon's cut. The faire is open."

doneWhen.en: Every student is at a booth or in the aisle and the room is quiet enough to hear you.
doneWhen.es: Every student is at a booth or in the aisle and the room is quiet enough to hear you.

watchFor.en: A rush to the nearest booth. Hold them for the full lap.
watchFor.es: A rush to the nearest booth. Hold them for the full lap.

description.en: Teacher "cuts ribbon" to open the faire Brief reminder of shopping etiquette and booth responsibilities
description.es: Teacher "cuts ribbon" to open the faire Brief reminder of shopping etiquette and booth responsibilities

sayThis.en: "Ten dollars a token, and you're carrying about a hundred. Sellers, write every sale down as it happens. You will not remember at the end, and the numbers matter."
sayThis.es: "Ten dollars a token, and you're carrying about a hundred. Sellers, write every sale down as it happens. You will not remember at the end, and the numbers matter."

doneWhen.en: Every booth's sales log has at least one line and every shopper has spent or decided not to.
doneWhen.es: Every booth's sales log has at least one line and every shopper has spent or decided not to.

watchFor.en: Sales going unrecorded in the rush. Ring a bell at four minutes and make everyone write.
watchFor.es: Sales going unrecorded in the rush. Ring a bell at four minutes and make everyone write.

description.en: Half class shops with 10-15 tokens worth $10 each ($100-150), half manages booths. Record every sale on log.
description.es: Half class shops with 10-15 tokens worth $10 each ($100-150), half manages booths. Record every sale on log.

sayThis.en: "Swap over. Sellers are shoppers now. You've watched how people buy for eight minutes — use it. Prices can change."
sayThis.es: "Swap over. Sellers are shoppers now. You've watched how people buy for eight minutes — use it. Prices can change."

doneWhen.en: Every booth has a new seller and Period 2 sales are being logged.
doneWhen.es: Every booth has a new seller and Period 2 sales are being logged.

watchFor.en: New sellers who don't know the prices on the booth they inherited. Give ten seconds for a handover.
watchFor.es: New sellers who don't know the prices on the booth they inherited. Give ten seconds for a handover.

description.en: Roles reverse. Continue shopping and selling.
description.es: Roles reverse. Continue shopping and selling.

sayThis.en: "Count your tokens. Times ten. That's your revenue. Take off what your materials cost. What's left is profit — and the profit is the number that matters, not how many you sold."
sayThis.es: "Count your tokens. Times ten. That's your revenue. Take off what your materials cost. What's left is profit — and the profit is the number that matters, not how many you sold."

doneWhen.en: Every Business Report shows revenue, material cost and profit.
doneWhen.es: Every Business Report shows revenue, material cost and profit.

watchFor.en: Tokens counted as dollars. They're ten each. Do the first conversion on the board.
watchFor.es: Tokens counted as dollars. They're ten each. Do the first conversion on the board.

description.en: Count all tokens collected and convert to dollars at $10 each - Review sales logs (how many items sold?) - Calculate profit using worksheet: Revenue − Material Costs = Profit - Record results on Business Report. Tier 1 (K-1): count tokens by tens — 10, 20, 30 — and skip the cost math.
description.es: Count all tokens collected and convert to dollars at $10 each - Review sales logs (how many items sold?) - Calculate profit using worksheet: Revenue − Material Costs = Profit - Record results on Business Report. Tier 1 (K-1): count tokens by tens — 10, 20, 30 — and skip the cost math.

sayThis.en: "Six awards, and only one of them is about money. Design. Display. Sales. Most creative. Best service. Most improved. When I call your name, come and get it."
sayThis.es: "Six awards, and only one of them is about money. Design. Display. Sales. Most creative. Best service. Most improved. When I call your name, come and get it."

doneWhen.en: All six certificates have been read out and handed over.
doneWhen.es: All six certificates have been read out and handed over.

watchFor.en: Rushing the names. Slow down and let each one land.
watchFor.es: Rushing the names. Slow down and let each one land.

description.en: Present certificates: Best Product Design, Best Display, Most Sales, Most Creative Item, Best Customer Service, Most Improved Maker
description.es: Present certificates: Best Product Design, Best Display, Most Sales, Most Creative Item, Best Customer Service, Most Improved Maker

sayThis.en: "One sentence, round the circle. The most important thing I learned as a maker is — and you finish it."
sayThis.es: "One sentence, round the circle. The most important thing I learned as a maker is — and you finish it."

doneWhen.en: Every student in the circle has finished the sentence out loud.
doneWhen.es: Every student in the circle has finished the sentence out loud.

watchFor.en: Repeats of whatever the last person said. Ask for one nobody has said yet.
watchFor.es: Repeats of whatever the last person said. Ask for one nobody has said yet.

description.en: Circle share: "The most important thing I learned as a maker is ___."
description.es: Circle share: "The most important thing I learned as a maker is ___."

discussionQuestions: What strategies did you use to attract customers to your booth?
Which products sold out? What made them popular?
How did your pricing compare to others? Was yours higher or lower? Why?
Looking at your profit, was your business successful?
If you did this faire again, what would you do differently?
Which skill you learned this season (woodworking, pottery, invention, design) was most valuable?
How did the market research from CH10 help you know what to make?
What's the difference between revenue and profit? Why does that matter?
Would you want to be a real maker when you grow up? Why or why not?
extensionIdeas: Invite another class or families to attend the faire as customers
Create "Makers' Portfolio" with photos of all products from the season
Write reflective essays: "My Journey as a Maker"
Research real makers' faires (Maker Faire Bay Area, local craft markets) and compare
Plan a Season 4 business based on the products that sold best
Create video "commercials" for products before the faire

beforeClass.en: Count paper clip tokens into shopper bundles of 10 to 15 before class. Each token is worth $10, so one bundle is $100 to $150. Decide where the booths go so the room can actually be walked.
beforeClass.es: Count paper clip tokens into shopper bundles of 10 to 15 before class. Each token is worth $10, so one bundle is $100 to $150. Decide where the booths go so the room can actually be walked.

runningLongOrShort.en: Long: run one shopping period of twelve minutes instead of two. Short: add a clearance round at the end where unsold items get marked down.
runningLongOrShort.es: Long: run one shopping period of twelve minutes instead of two. Short: add a clearance round at the end where unsold items get marked down.

items: Paper clips, 1 box of 500, as the payment tokens — $2.50. Counted back in and reused

Student-made items from the earlier Season 3 chapters as the inventory
